symbols.name: V
symbols.def: The finite substantive-variable set of the labeled-missingness system.

symbols.name: R
symbols.type: finite set of binary missingness indicators
symbols.def: The indicators whose value zero denotes that the corresponding partially observed substantive variable is missing.

symbols.name: Vdag
symbols.type: finite set of observed proxy variables
symbols.def: The proxy copy of each partially observed variable, equal to its substantive value when observed and to the missing symbol otherwise.

symbols.name: O
symbols.def: The complete observed record consisting of always-observed substantive variables, proxies, and missingness indicators.

symbols.name: Xspace
symbols.def: The finite alphabet assigned to each substantive, indicator, and proxy variable.

symbols.name: A
symbols.def: The treatment whose natural causal effect is queried.

symbols.name: Y
symbols.def: The outcome of the intervention on \(A\).

symbols.name: sY
symbols.def: A supplied real-valued coding of the finite outcome alphabet used to form the natural average treatment contrast.

symbols.name: a0
symbols.def: The reference treatment value \(a_0\).

symbols.name: a1
symbols.def: The active treatment value \(a_1\), distinct from \(a_0\).

symbols.name: G
symbols.def: A known finite labeled-missingness graph whose directed part is acyclic, whose bidirected edges encode latent districts, and whose label set records the missingness contexts in which directed edges are absent.

symbols.name: Hlog
symbols.type: finite set of always-observed pre-treatment logistics variables
symbols.def: A nonempty always-observed DAG block whose only arrows to vertices outside the block enter the missingness indicator \(R_W\).

symbols.name: C
symbols.def: A member of \(H\) with the arrow \(C\to R_W\).

symbols.name: Bchain
symbols.type: finite chain of always-observed mediator variables
symbols.def: The mediator chain \(A\to B_1\to\cdots\to B_m\to Y\) used by the endogenous-indicator proxy front-door family.

symbols.name: M
symbols.def: A measurable semi-Markovian structural model in the published ambient class compatible with \(\mathcal G\), with one mutually independent latent factor for each individual bidirected edge and one private factor for each vertex, including its proxy equations and label-specific mechanism deletions.

symbols.name: Mlm
symbols.def: The de Aguas--Henckel--Pensar--Biele ambient class of measurable categorical-or-continuous semi-Markovian labeled-missingness SCMs inducing \(\mathcal G\); finite endogenous alphabets, strict full-data positivity, and regular-maximality are additional restrictions of the TCF subclass.

symbols.name: Mplus
symbols.def: The finite strictly positive regular-maximal subclass of \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{lm}}(\mathcal G)\) used by the recovery problem.

symbols.name: Pobs
symbols.def: A population law of the observed record \(\mathcal O\).

symbols.name: pCell
symbols.def: Algebraically independent real variables subject to the observed-simplex and compatibility formulas; specialization sets \(p_o=P_{\mathrm{obs}}(o)\).

symbols.name: ExactObs
symbols.def: Either rational observed cells, real-algebraic observed cells given by square-free integer polynomials and rational isolating intervals, or an exact-real oracle that decides the sign of every integer polynomial at the observed-cell vector.

symbols.name: Fiber
symbols.def: The models in \(\mathfrak M_{+}^{\mathrm{rm}}(\mathcal G)\) that induce the same observed proxy law \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\).

symbols.name: Qa
symbols.def: The natural interventional distribution of \(Y\) under treatment value \(a\), retaining the endogenous missingness mechanism shifts.

symbols.name: tau
symbols.def: The score-coded natural average treatment effect obtained from the two interventional outcome laws.

symbols.name: kappa
symbols.def: A current CADMG \(\mathcal H\), fixed set \(F\), context assignment \(c\), kernel \(q\), observed-law provenance expression \(\pi\), and ordered label-license trace \(\Lambda\).

symbols.name: Fix
symbols.def: The nested fixing update for a vertex \(v\), tagged by the label license \(\lambda\) and retaining its pre-restriction observed-law trace.

symbols.name: Select
symbols.def: The update that restricts a trace-aware state to missingness context \(c\) only after recording every kernel factor derived before restriction.

symbols.name: Swap
symbols.def: The primitive adjacent-swap condition that \(u\) and \(v\) are both fixable in \(\mathcal H\), neither is an ancestor of a missingness variable appearing in the other's license, and both denominator traces are supported before the same context restriction.

symbols.name: LatentIndex
symbols.def: One factor index for each individual bidirected edge of \(\mathcal G\), plus one private factor for each substantive or missingness vertex; all indexed factors are mutually independent.

symbols.name: Krf
symbols.def: Here \(L_{\mathcal G}=|\mathcal X_{\mathcal V}\times\mathcal X_{\mathcal R}|\). After factorwise support reduction, every individual bidirected-edge and private factor may be assigned the alphabet \(\{1,\ldots,K_{\mathrm{ub}}(\mathcal G)\}\). This is a universal upper bound, not a claimed sharp bound.

symbols.name: Resp
symbols.type: finite set of label-compatible vertex response-table tuples
symbols.def: Each \(g=(g_Z)_Z\in\mathcal T_{\mathcal G}\) is a tuple of deterministic maps from the observed-parent values, the private latent state, and the states of the individual bidirected-edge factors incident to \(Z\) into \(\mathcal X_Z\), with table entries identified exactly when a graph label requires an observed parent to be omitted in that context.

symbols.name: gamma
symbols.def: Real variables constrained by \(\gamma_g^2-\gamma_g=0\) and \(\sum_g\gamma_g=1\), so exactly one label-compatible structural-table tuple is selected and no mixture across graph-wide tables is introduced.

symbols.name: rho
symbols.sig: \(\rho=(\rho_{h,k}:h\in\mathcal E^{\leftrightarrow}(\mathcal G)\sqcup\mathcal V\sqcup\mathcal R,\ 1\leq k\leq K_{\mathrm{ub}}(\mathcal G))\)
symbols.def: For every individual bidirected-edge or private factor \(h\), the coordinates satisfy \(\rho_{h,k}\geq0\) and \(\sum_{k=1}^{K_{\mathrm{ub}}(\mathcal G)}\rho_{h,k}=1\); the probability of a joint latent state is the product over \(h\).

symbols.name: theta
symbols.def: The one-hot table selectors together with the mutually independent individual-edge and private-factor weights.

symbols.name: pRF
symbols.def: The sum over the finite latent-factor states and selected structural table of the product \(\gamma_g\prod_h\rho_{h,u_h}\) when deterministic evaluation gives full-data cell \((v,r)\), and its proxy-consistent sum over cells mapping to observed cell \(o\).

symbols.name: qRF
symbols.def: The same independent-factor polynomial sum after replacing the selected response equation for \(A\) by the constant \(a\) and summing all remaining finite cells with \(Y=y\).

symbols.name: Compat
symbols.def: The conjunction of one-hot table equations, one simplex for every individual latent factor, strict positivity of every full-data cell polynomial, and the equalities \(p_o(\theta)=p_o\) for all observed cells.

symbols.name: ConstTest
symbols.type: first-order real-closed-field formula with observed-law parameters
symbols.def: The first-order real-closed-field formula denying two \(\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}(\cdot;\mathbf p)\)-compatible response vectors with unequal \(q_{a,y}\) values, leaving only \(\mathbf p\) free.

symbols.name: SemiPart
symbols.def: A finite family of pairwise-disjoint quantifier-free sign formulas whose union is the compatible observed-law projection and whose cells carry, for every \(a,y\), either a unique-value graph formula or a non-singleton-fiber witness formula.

symbols.name: AlgPair
symbols.def: On a negative partition cell, the compatibility conjunction for two response vectors together with \(q_{a,y}(\theta^0)\neq q_{a,y}(\theta^1)\); exact specialization yields a sample \(\omega=(a,y,\theta^0,\theta^1)\) represented by Thom encodings over the ordered field generated by \(\mathbf p\), and the coordinates are real algebraic when the observed cells are rational or real algebraic.

symbols.name: TCF
symbols.def: The observed-law-indexed trace-aware colored fixing compiler that treats the cells of \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) as formal coordinates \(\mathbf p\) and returns the finite semialgebraic decision object \(\mathscr P_{\mathcal G,A,Y}\); an exact-law specialization selects a unique cell and yields its functional or algebraic witness formula. Colored hedges are not part of this output contract.

symbols.name: Fobs
symbols.def: On an identifying cell of \(\mathscr P_{\mathcal G,A,Y}\), either a rational trace expression or the unique real-algebraic value whose graph is specified by a quantifier-free polynomial formula; exact specialization uses isolating data only when needed.

symbols.name: DA4
symbols.type: set of de Aguas Proposition 4 certificates
symbols.def: The triples \(\xi=(K,H,\{L_r:r\in\operatorname{supp}(R_K)\})\) satisfying Proposition 4 conditions \(\mathrm{(i)}\)--\(\mathrm{(v)}\) in the labeled graphs \(\mathcal G_r\) and \(\mathcal H_r\).

symbols.name: FDA4
symbols.def: The published weighted context formula \(\sum_r P_{\mathrm{obs}}(R_K=r)\sum_{\ell}P_{\mathrm{obs}}(L_r^{\dagger}=\ell\mid R_K=r,R_{M_r}=1)P_{\mathrm{obs}}(Y=y\mid A=a,L_r^{\dagger}=\ell,R_K=r,R_{M_r}=1,R_H=0)\).

symbols.name: RootCtx
symbols.def: A certificate that every label context variable is an observed causal root and that the Mokhtarian--Jamshidi--Etesami--Kiyavash context-by-context algorithm identifies the interventional law in every context DAG.

symbols.name: FRoot
symbols.def: The sum over root-control contexts of the published context-specific ID functional multiplied by the observed probability of that context.

symbols.name: CH
symbols.def: The nested rooted-forest obstructions equipped with compatible missingness colors and complete observed-trace provenance.

symbols.name: Divergence
symbols.def: A testable predicate requiring agreement of all proper-predecessor trace polynomials, \(D\subsetneq D'\), equal roots ancestral to \(Y\) after intervention, \(D\cap A=\varnothing\), \(D'\cap A\neq\varnothing\), and persistence of the query-polynomial difference after marginalizing outside \(D'\). It does not assert that a qualifying record exists or implies a colored hedge.

symbols.name: Compiler
symbols.def: A finite syntax-directed procedure that decodes the two edge-factorized response models and returns either the first retained-history record passing the candidate divergence tests or an exhaustion tag. It does not return or certify a colored hedge.

symbols.name: M0
symbols.def: The first edge-factorized response model decoded from an exact negative-cell sample.

symbols.name: M1
symbols.def: The second edge-factorized response model decoded from an exact negative-cell sample.

symbols.name: GFig
symbols.def: The de Aguas et al. Figure 3(b) graph with \(R_W\to A\), \(Z\to A\), \(Z\to W\), \(W\to A\) labeled by \(R_W=0\), \(W\leftrightarrow Y\), \(R_Z\leftrightarrow Y\), and \(A\to Y\).

symbols.name: PFig
symbols.type: observed proxy law on the Figure 3(b) graph
symbols.def: A strictly positive observed law compatible with \(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{3b}}\).

symbols.name: GEIP
symbols.def: The parameterized family obtained from the Figure 3(b) fix-before-select module by adding a nonempty always-observed logistics DAG \(H\) with an arrow \(C\to R_W\), replacing \(A\to Y\) by the mediator chain \(A\to B_1\to\cdots\to B_m\to Y\), and adding \(A\leftrightarrow Y\).

symbols.name: GStar
symbols.def: The member with one logistics parent \(C\to R_W\), one mediator \(A\to B_1\to Y\), the Figure 3(b) edges and proxy mechanism, and the added edge \(A\leftrightarrow Y\).

symbols.name: FStar
symbols.def: The observed-law functional obtained by averaging the conditional front-door formula in context \(R_W=0\) over the marginal law of \(C\).

symbols.name: Size
symbols.def: Here \(n=|\mathcal V\cup\mathcal R\cup\mathcal V^{\dagger}|\), \(\ell=|\mathcal L|\), \(c=\prod_{R_Z\in\mathcal R}(|\mathcal X_{R_Z}|+1)\), \(h=|\mathcal E^{\leftrightarrow}(\mathcal G)|+|\mathcal V|+|\mathcal R|\), \(g=|\mathcal T_{\mathcal G}|\), \(K_{\mathrm{ub}}(\mathcal G)\) is the universal factor-support upper bound, \(p=2\{g+hK_{\mathrm{ub}}(\mathcal G)\}+|\mathcal X_{\mathcal O}|\), and \(s\) is the maximum of the complete binary encoding length of the single base-CAD input and any one whole-cell candidate-verification sentence, including polynomial counts, degrees, integer coefficients, variable indices, Boolean connectives, and the names of all free observed cells.

symbols.name: CADsteps
symbols.def: For a fixed signed-subresultant cylindrical-algebraic-decomposition implementation, the maximum of its number of projection, real-root-isolation, sign-evaluation steps and output cells over real-closed-field formulas with at most \(m\) total quantified-plus-free variables and binary encoding length at most \(b\).

symbols.name: eps
symbols.def: The probability used by a label-preserving response randomization when strict positivity is imposed on a finite witness.

symbols.name: RFHandle
symbols.def: The label-respecting response-function encoding attached to a colored hedge and a positivity parameter.

assumptions.condition: \(|\mathcal X_Z|<\infty\) for every \(Z\in\mathcal V\cup\mathcal R\cup\mathcal V^{\dagger}\).
The directed part of \(\mathcal G\) is acyclic.

\(\mathcal M\) has one exogenous factor shared by the two endpoints of each bidirected edge of \(\mathcal G\), one private exogenous factor for each substantive or missingness vertex, and all these factors are mutually independent.
For every partially observed \(Z\in\mathcal V\), \(Z^{\dagger}=Z\) when \(R_Z=1\) and \(Z^{\dagger}=\star\) when \(R_Z=0\).
Every label \((X,Z,R_X=0)\) in \(\mathcal G\) encodes that the structural mechanism for \(Z\) omits \(X\) in context \(R_X=0\).
The label set of \(\mathcal G\) is regular.
The label set of \(\mathcal G\) is maximal.
\(P_{\mathcal M}(v,r)>0\) for every \((v,r)\in\mathcal X_{\mathcal V}\times\mathcal X_{\mathcal R}\).

standard.name: strict positivity for finite causal laws

definitions.name: Published labeled-missingness SCM class
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{lm}}(\mathcal G)\) is the published ambient class of semi-Markovian labeled-missingness SCMs on the finite vertex graph \(\mathcal G\): endogenous and exogenous state spaces may be measurable categorical or continuous standard Borel spaces, structural maps are measurable, the individual bidirected-edge and private exogenous factors are mutually independent, the proxy equations satisfy proxy consistency, and every labeled mechanism deletion has the semantics encoded by \(\mathcal G\). Finiteness of endogenous alphabets, strict positivity of every full-data cell, and regular-maximality are not part of this ambient definition.

definitions.name: Positive regular-maximal labeled-missingness class
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak M_{+}^{\mathrm{rm}}(\mathcal G)=\{\mathcal M\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{lm}}(\mathcal G):|\mathcal X_Z|<\infty\text{ for every }Z\in\mathcal V\cup\mathcal R\cup\mathcal V^{\dagger},\ \mathcal G\text{ is regular and maximal},\ P_{\mathcal M}(v,r)>0\text{ for every }(v,r)\in\mathcal X_{\mathcal V}\times\mathcal X_{\mathcal R}\}\).

definitions.name: Observed-proxy-law fiber
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak F(\mathcal G,P_{\mathrm{obs}})=\{\mathcal M\in\mathfrak M_{+}^{\mathrm{rm}}(\mathcal G):P_{\mathcal M}(\mathcal O)=P_{\mathrm{obs}}\}\).

definitions.name: Natural interventional law and contrast
definitions.construction: For \(a\in\mathcal X_A\), set \(Q_a^{\mathcal M}(y)=P_{\mathcal M}(Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(A=a))\), and set \(\tau_{s_Y}=\sum_{y\in\mathcal X_Y}s_Y(y)\{Q_{a_1}^{\mathcal M}(y)-Q_{a_0}^{\mathcal M}(y)\}\).

definitions.name: Edge-factorized finite response-function polynomial fiber
definitions.construction:
Let
\[
L_{\mathcal G}=\left|\mathcal X_{\mathcal V}\times\mathcal X_{\mathcal R}\right|,
\qquad
K_{\mathrm{ub}}(\mathcal G)=L_{\mathcal G}+|\mathcal X_A|(|\mathcal X_Y|-1),
\qquad
\mathcal J=\mathcal E^{\leftrightarrow}(\mathcal G)\sqcup\mathcal V\sqcup\mathcal R.
\]
The integer \(K_{\mathrm{ub}}(\mathcal G)\) is a universal factorwise upper bound, not a claimed sharp support size. For \(g\in\mathcal T_{\mathcal G}\) introduce \(\gamma_g\), and for \(h\in\mathcal J\) and \(1\leq k\leq K_{\mathrm{ub}}(\mathcal G)\) introduce \(\rho_{h,k}\). For a full cell \((v,r)\), define
\[
p_{v,r}(\theta)=
\sum_{g\in\mathcal T_{\mathcal G}}
\sum_{u\in\{1,\ldots,K_{\mathrm{ub}}(\mathcal G)\}^{\mathcal J}}
\mathbf 1\{g(u)=(v,r)\}\gamma_g\prod_{h\in\mathcal J}\rho_{h,u_h},
\qquad
p_o(\theta)=\sum_{(v,r):\operatorname{proxy}(v,r)=o}p_{v,r}(\theta).
\]
Define \(q_{a,y}(\theta)\) by the same product sum after replacing the selected equation for \(A\) by the constant \(a\). With formal observed coordinates \(\mathbf p=(p_o)_o\), set
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}(\theta;\mathbf p):={}&
\bigwedge_{g\in\mathcal T_{\mathcal G}}(\gamma_g^2-\gamma_g=0)
\ \wedge\ \sum_g\gamma_g=1\\
&\wedge\bigwedge_{h\in\mathcal J}
\left(\bigwedge_{k=1}^{K_{\mathrm{ub}}(\mathcal G)}\rho_{h,k}\geq0
\ \wedge\ \sum_{k=1}^{K_{\mathrm{ub}}(\mathcal G)}\rho_{h,k}=1\right)\\
&\wedge\bigwedge_{(v,r)}p_{v,r}(\theta)>0
\ \wedge\ \bigwedge_{o\in\mathcal X_{\mathcal O}}p_o(\theta)=p_o.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus every individual bidirected-edge or private factor has its own simplex and the joint latent law is the product over \(h\). The one-hot equations select one graph-wide tuple of label-compatible deterministic tables; they do not mix structural tables through an additional unrestricted district latent.

definitions.name: Symbolic terminal real-closed-field constancy test
definitions.construction: For every \(a\in\mathcal X_A\) and \(y\in\mathcal X_Y\), use disjoint copies \(\theta^0=(\gamma^0,\rho^0)\) and \(\theta^1=(\gamma^1,\rho^1)\) and eliminate precisely those response variables from \[\mathsf I_{a,y}(\mathcal G;\mathbf p):=\neg\exists\theta^0\,\exists\theta^1\left[\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}(\theta^0;\mathbf p)\wedge\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}(\theta^1;\mathbf p)\wedge q_{a,y}(\theta^0)\neq q_{a,y}(\theta^1)\right].\] The only free variables are the \(|\mathcal X_{\mathcal O}|\) coordinates \(\mathbf p\). Quantifier elimination returns a quantifier-free sign formula, not a numerical decision at an arbitrary population law. On its true region the value relation is \[\mathsf V_{a,y}(\mathbf p,z):=\exists\theta\left[\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}(\theta;\mathbf p)\wedge z=q_{a,y}(\theta)\right],\] which has exactly one \(z\); on its false region the certificate formula is the unnegated doubled conjunction. A sample pair is extracted only after an exact specialization.

definitions.name: Symbolic observed-law decision partition
definitions.construction: Conjoin the simplex formula \(p_o\geq0\), \(\sum_op_o=1\), and the feasible-projection formula \(\exists\theta\,\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}(\theta;\mathbf p)\) with every quantifier-free output of \(\mathsf I_{a,y}\), refine their common sign-invariant CAD, and discard infeasible cells. The remaining pairwise-disjoint formulas \(\psi_1(\mathbf p),\ldots,\psi_J(\mathbf p)\) form \(\mathscr P_{\mathcal G,A,Y}\). Each cell stores, for every \(a,y\), either the unique-value relation \(\mathsf V_{a,y}(\mathbf p,z)\) or the witness relation \(\mathsf W_j(\mathbf p,a,y,\theta^0,\theta^1)\).

definitions.name: Exact observed-law specialization
definitions.construction: Given \(\operatorname{Exact}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\), decide the finitely many integer-polynomial signs in \(\mathscr P_{\mathcal G,A,Y}\) using rational arithmetic, algebraic-number arithmetic with the supplied square-free polynomials and isolating intervals, or the supplied exact-real sign oracle. Choose the unique cell containing \(p_o=P_{\mathrm{obs}}(o)\). On an identifying cell, represent its unique value \(z\), and on a negative cell choose \(\theta^0,\theta^1\) satisfying \(\mathsf W_j\), by Thom encodings over the real closure of the ordered field generated by the specialized coordinates \(\mathbf p\). These response coordinates are algebraic over that ordered input field; they are real algebraic over \(\mathbb Q\) when the observed cells are rational or real algebraic, but no such claim is made for transcendental exact-real cells. No operation on an arbitrary unencoded population real is defined.

definitions.name: Published Proposition 4 certificate and functional
definitions.construction: \(\operatorname{DA4}(\mathcal G,A,Y)\) consists of every \(\xi=(K,H,\{L_r\}_r)\) satisfying de Aguas et al. Proposition 4 conditions \(\mathrm{(i)}\)--\(\mathrm{(v)}\): the inclusion and exclusion rule for \(L_r\), the no-descendant condition in \(\mathcal G_r\), and the three stated d-separations in \(\mathcal G_r[\overline A]\) and \(\mathcal H_r[\underline A]\). For such \(\xi\), \[f^{\mathrm{DA4}}_{a,\xi}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)=\sum_{r\in\operatorname{supp}(R_K)}P_{\mathrm{obs}}(R_K=r)\sum_{\ell}P_{\mathrm{obs}}(L_r^{\dagger}=\ell\mid R_K=r,R_{M_r}=1)P_{\mathrm{obs}}(Y=y\mid A=a,L_r^{\dagger}=\ell,R_K=r,R_{M_r}=1,R_H=0).\]

definitions.name: Published root-control certificate and functional
definitions.construction: \(\operatorname{RC}(\mathcal G,A,Y)\) holds when every label context variable is observed and parentless and the published context-specific algorithm returns \(f_{a,c}^{\mathrm{ID}}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)\) in every context \(c\). Its published aggregate is \[f_a^{\mathrm{RC}}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)=\sum_c P_{\mathrm{obs}}(C=c)f_{a,c}^{\mathrm{ID}}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y).\]

definitions.name: Trace-aware colored reachable state
definitions.construction: \(\kappa=(\mathcal H,F,c,q,\pi,\Lambda)\), where \(\mathcal H\) is the current CADMG, \(F\) is its fixed set, \(c\) is a partial assignment to missingness indicators, \(q\) is a normalized kernel on the random vertices of \(\mathcal H\), \(\pi\) is a finite expression in observed cells of \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\), and \(\Lambda\) is an ordered list of pairs consisting of a label license and the pre-restriction trace that licensed it.

definitions.name: Licensed colored fixing
definitions.construction: If \(v\) is fixable in \(\mathcal H\) and license \(\lambda\) is valid on the trace recorded by \(\kappa\), \(\Phi_v^{\lambda}\) moves \(v\) from the random to the fixed set, deletes arrowheads into \(v\), replaces \(q\) by \(q/q(v\mid\operatorname{mb}_{\mathcal H}(v))\), applies the same division to \(\pi\), and appends \(\lambda\) and its current provenance to \(\Lambda\).

definitions.name: Delayed context restriction
definitions.construction: For a missingness assignment \(c'\) compatible with the current trace, \(\Sigma_{c'}(\kappa)\) restricts \(q\) and \(\pi\) to \(c'\), normalizes on the positive selected cell, deletes the edges carrying labels activated by \(c'\), and retains every earlier entry of \(\Lambda\).

definitions.name: Primitive colored adjacent-swap condition
definitions.construction: \(\operatorname{Swap}_{\kappa}(u,v)\) holds exactly when \(u\) and \(v\) are both fixable in the current \(\mathcal H\), \(u\notin\operatorname{an}_{\mathcal H}(C_v)\), \(v\notin\operatorname{an}_{\mathcal H}(C_u)\), the license contexts \(C_u\) and \(C_v\) agree on their common indicators, and both fixing denominators are supported in the same pre-restriction trace.

definitions.name: Trace-colored hedge
definitions.construction: \(\operatorname{CH}(\mathcal G,A,Y)\) is the set of tuples \((\mathcal F,\mathcal F',\chi,T)\) such that \(\mathcal F'\subseteq\mathcal F\) are equally rooted \(C\)-forests, \(\mathcal F\cap A\neq\varnothing\), \(\mathcal F'\cap A=\varnothing\), their roots are ancestors of \(Y\) after intervention on \(A\), \(\chi\) assigns every label-sensitive edge its missingness context, and \(T\) is a prefix-closed collection of observed traces on which every color used by the two forests is licensed.

definitions.name: Algebraic-witness diagnostic compiler
definitions.construction: Given an exact specialized negative-cell witness \(\omega=(a,y,\theta^0,\theta^1)\) and a finite retained operation history \(\mathcal T\), first decode \(\theta^0,\theta^1\) through their selected response tables and product laws over the individual edge and private factors, obtaining \(\mathcal M_0,\mathcal M_1\). Next enumerate, in a fixed prefix and vertex-subset order, every triple \((\kappa_*,D,D')\) occurring in \(\mathcal T\) and test the conjuncts of the candidate predicate \(\Delta(\omega,\mathcal T)=(\kappa_*,D,D')\). Trace equalities are tested after clearing the supported nonzero denominators, using the Thom encodings supplied by exact specialization. Return \((\operatorname{found}(\kappa_*,D,D'),\mathcal M_0,\mathcal M_1)\) for the first successful test and return \((\operatorname{exhausted},\mathcal M_0,\mathcal M_1)\) if the finite enumeration ends. This is a partial graphical diagnostic: neither tag asserts existence of a colored hedge, membership in \(\operatorname{CH}(\mathcal G,A,Y)\), realization of a forest by the decoded models, or alignment of the algebraic sample with a graphwise recursion failure.

definitions.name: Trace-aware colored fixing procedure
definitions.construction:
On formal input \((\mathcal G,A,Y,\mathbf p)\), first construct the response-polynomial feasibility formula \(\exists\theta\,\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}(\theta;\mathbf p)\) and the coordinate-constancy formulas \(\mathsf I_{a,y}(\mathcal G;\mathbf p)\) for all \((a,y)\). Run one common signed-subresultant CAD on this base family alone, retaining \(\mathbf p\), to obtain the canonical cells \(\psi_j\) and their unique-value or witness relations. This base partition is independent of every fixing trace.

After the base cells have been fixed, enumerate expression-discovery traces. Start from every supported observed margin and partial-context trace kernel written as a rational expression in \(\mathbf p\). Recursively branch only by strict ancestral marginalization, restriction to a proper child of a nontrivial district decomposition, a licensed \(\Phi_v^{\lambda}\) update, or a delayed \(\Sigma_{c'}\) update that strictly extends the partial context. Retain the complete operation word and memoize only literal complete tuples \(\kappa=(\mathcal H,F,c,q,\pi,\Lambda)\), including the syntax of \(q\), \(\pi\), and every provenance entry in \(\Lambda\). An adjacent-swap optimization may merge branches only after replaying both license orders from their common pre-swap state in a fixed canonical order and verifying literal equality of the complete resulting tuples. Fixing and selection are never commuted.

For a candidate trace expression \(r(\mathbf p)=N(\mathbf p)/D(\mathbf p)\), a base cell \(\psi_j\), and a coordinate \((a,y)\) whose cell relation is unique, use real-closed-field quantifier elimination to decide the whole-cell implication
\[
\forall\mathbf p\,\forall z\,
\left[
\psi_j(\mathbf p)\wedge\mathsf V_{a,y}(\mathbf p,z)
\ \Longrightarrow\ D(\mathbf p)\neq0\ \wedge\ D(\mathbf p)z=N(\mathbf p)
\right].
\]
Annotate \(\psi_j\) by \(r\) only if this implication is true. If no candidate passes, retain the unique-value graph \(\mathsf V_{a,y}\); on a nonconstant cell retain \(\mathsf W_j\). Trace enumeration and annotation never split, merge, or otherwise alter the base CAD cells. The notation \(\operatorname{TCF}(\mathcal G,A,Y,P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) denotes this symbolic partition and its verified annotations with formal names \(p_o=P_{\mathrm{obs}}(o)\). Numerical cell selection is the separate exact specialization. The procedure neither names nor returns a colored hedge.

definitions.name: Figure 3(b) fix-then-select instance
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{3b}}\) has substantive vertices \(\{A,Y,Z,W\}\), indicators \(\{R_W,R_Z\}\), their observed proxies, arrows \(R_W\to A\), \(Z\to A\), \(Z\to W\), \(W\to A\), \(A\to Y\), edges \(W\leftrightarrow Y\) and \(R_Z\leftrightarrow Y\), and label \(R_W=0\) on \(W\to A\); \(P_{\mathrm{3b}}\) is any compatible strictly positive observed law.

definitions.name: Endogenous-indicator proxy front-door class
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak G_{\mathrm{EIPFD}}=\{\mathcal G(H,m):H\in\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{log}},\ m\geq1\}\), where \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{log}}\) is the set of nonempty finite always-observed DAGs with at least one \(C\to R_W\) and with no arrow from \(H\) to a vertex outside \(H\cup\{R_W\}\). Each \(\mathcal G(H,m)\) contains the Figure 3(b) module on \(A,Y,Z,W,R_W,R_Z\), replaces \(A\to Y\) by \(A\to B_1\to\cdots\to B_m\to Y\), adds \(A\leftrightarrow Y\), retains \(W^{\dagger}\), and keeps the label \(R_W=0\) on \(W\to A\). All \(B_j\) and all vertices of \(H\) are always observed. The member \(\mathcal G_\star=\mathcal G(\{C\},1)\) has exactly the additional vertices \(C,B_1\) and arrows \(C\to R_W\), \(A\to B_1\to Y\), and \(A\leftrightarrow Y\).

definitions.name: Worked delayed-selection front-door functional
definitions.construction: For \(\mathcal G_\star=\mathcal G(\{C\},1)\), define \[f_a^\star(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)=\sum_{c\in\mathcal X_C}P_{\mathrm{obs}}(c)\sum_{b\in\mathcal X_{B_1}}P_{\mathrm{obs}}(b\mid a,c,R_W=0)\sum_{a'\in\mathcal X_A}P_{\mathrm{obs}}(y\mid b,a',c,R_W=0)P_{\mathrm{obs}}(a'\mid c,R_W=0).\] The operation order attached to this expression is: derive \(P(Y\mid\operatorname{do}(A),R_W)\) with its pre-selection trace, select \(R_W=0\), apply front-door adjustment through \(B_1\) conditional on \(C\), and average using the unselected marginal \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}(C)\).

definitions.name: Finite history and quantifier-elimination budget
definitions.construction:
For the size quantities \((n,\ell,c,h,g,K_{\mathrm{ub}}(\mathcal G),p,s)\), define
\[
L_{\mathrm{op}}=2^{n+1}+n(\ell+1)+c+1,
\qquad
B_{\mathrm{state}}=2^n c\sum_{j=0}^{2n}L_{\mathrm{op}}^j.
\]
Here \(2^n c\) bounds the initial observed-margin and partial-context traces, and the operation alphabet bounds ancestral and district subset choices, vertex-license choices, strict context extensions, and one harmless terminal marker. The recursive word length \(2n\) counts every provenance-bearing marginalization, district restriction, fixing, and selection in its actual order.

Let
\[
p=2\{g+hK_{\mathrm{ub}}(\mathcal G)\}+|\mathcal X_{\mathcal O}|.
\]
Let \(s\) be the maximum of the complete binary encoding length of the single trace-independent base feasibility/coordinate-constancy CAD input and the complete binary encoding length of any one whole-cell candidate-verification sentence generated by an operation word of length at most \(2n\), including its canonical cell formula, cleared numerator and denominator, polynomial counts, degrees, integer coefficients, variable indices, Boolean connectives, and free observed-cell names. Define
\[
C_{\mathrm{base}}=\operatorname{CAD}(p,s),
\qquad
N_{\mathrm{check}}=|\mathcal X_A||\mathcal X_Y|B_{\mathrm{state}}C_{\mathrm{base}},
\]
\[
B_{\mathrm{tot}}=
B_{\mathrm{state}}+C_{\mathrm{base}}
+N_{\mathrm{check}}\operatorname{CAD}(p+1,s).
\]
The first CAD is run once, before trace enumeration. Its number of output cells is at most \(C_{\mathrm{base}}\). Each subsequent annotation sentence uses at most one response vector, \(z\), and \(\mathbf p\), hence at most \(p+1\) variables, and no more than \(N_{\mathrm{check}}\) such sentences are tested. Exact point specialization is a separate finite sign computation under \(\operatorname{Exact}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\).

definitions.name: Binary positive colored-witness handle
definitions.construction: Begin with the response-function cells indexed by \((\mathcal F,\mathcal F',\chi,T)\in\operatorname{CH}(\mathcal G,A,Y)\); impose the polynomial equalities for every observed proxy trace and every color deletion; then use label-preserving output randomization with parameter \(\varepsilon\) and alphabet lifting to search for a two-state substantive encoding without specifying its response tables in advance.

statements.statement: \(\mathfrak M_{+}^{\mathrm{rm}}(\mathcal G)\subsetneq\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{lm}}(\mathcal G)\). The natural interventional law \(Q_a^{\mathcal M}\) and the score-coded NATE contrast \(\tau_{s_Y}\) are restrictions of the published natural-effect query to this subclass, and strictness is witnessed by any compatible finite lm-SCM with a zero full-data cell.
statements.justification: The inclusion pins the new theorem to the published lm-SCM semantics rather than to a bespoke analogue.
statements.gap: De Aguas et al. define the ambient lm-SCM class but do not isolate the finite positive regular-maximal subclass required by an exact recovery calculus.
statements.consumer: Applied NATE analyses can read every returned functional under the original published natural-effect interpretation.
statements.proof_tex:
We prove separately the inclusion, its strictness, and the restriction claim.

Let \(\mathcal M^{+}\in\mathfrak M_{+}^{\mathrm{rm}}(\mathcal G)\).  By the set-builder construction in Definition \texttt{def:positive-rm-class},
\[
\mathcal M^{+}\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{lm}}(\mathcal G).
\]
Since \(\mathcal M^{+}\) was arbitrary,
\[
\mathfrak M_{+}^{\mathrm{rm}}(\mathcal G)
\subseteq
\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{lm}}(\mathcal G).
\tag{1}
\]

We now exhibit why the inclusion is proper.  Start with a compatible finite lm-SCM \(\overline{\mathcal M}\) in the ambient class supplied by the model setup.  Write the treatment equation in this model as
\[
A=f_A\bigl(\operatorname{pa}_A,U_A,U_A^{\leftrightarrow}\bigr),
\tag{2}
\]
where \(U_A\) is the private treatment factor and \(U_A^{\leftrightarrow}\) is the tuple of edge-specific factors incident to \(A\).  Introduce the standard-Borel disjoint union
\[
\mathcal U_A^{0}=\{\bot_A\}\mathbin{\dot\cup}\mathcal U_A
\]
and give the new private factor \(U_A^{0}\) the point-mass law
\[
P(U_A^{0}=\bot_A)=1.
\tag{3}
\]
Replace only (2) by
\[
f_A^{0}(p,u,w)=
\begin{cases}
a_0,&u=\bot_A,\\
f_A(p,u,w),&u\in\mathcal U_A,
\end{cases}
\tag{4}
\]
and call the resulting model \(\mathcal M^{0}\).  All other structural equations, all edge-specific factors, and all proxy equations are left unchanged.  The joint exogenous law is the product of the point mass in (3) and the old laws of the remaining mutually independent factors, so \(\mathcal M^{0}\) is still semi-Markovian.  Equation (4) is measurable.  On every old branch \(u\in\mathcal U_A\) it is the old structural map, while on the added branch it is constant.  Thus it introduces no parent or latent dependence forbidden by \(\mathcal G\), and all old structurally permitted branches remain in the response map.  In particular, every label-specific deletion remains valid.  The unchanged proxy equations retain proxy consistency.  No causal-minimality, faithfulness, or positive-support condition is part of Definition \texttt{def:published-lm-class}.  Hence that definition yields
\[
\mathcal M^{0}\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{lm}}(\mathcal G).
\tag{5}
\]
The endogenous alphabets of \(\overline{\mathcal M}\) were finite and were not changed.

Equations (3)--(4) imply
\[
P_{\mathcal M^{0}}(A=a_0)=1.
\tag{6}
\]
Because \(a_1\ne a_0\), choose a full-data configuration \((v^{1},r^{1})\in\mathcal X_{\mathcal V}\times\mathcal X_{\mathcal R}\) whose \(A\)-coordinate is \(a_1\); all remaining coordinates can be selected from their nonempty state spaces.  Then (6) gives
\[
0\le P_{\mathcal M^{0}}(v^{1},r^{1})
\le P_{\mathcal M^{0}}(A=a_1)=0,
\]
and therefore
\[
P_{\mathcal M^{0}}(v^{1},r^{1})=0.
\tag{7}
\]
The strict-positivity clause of Definition \texttt{def:positive-rm-class} requires every such full-data cell to have positive probability.  Thus
\[
\mathcal M^{0}\notin\mathfrak M_{+}^{\mathrm{rm}}(\mathcal G).
\tag{8}
\]
Combining (5) and (8) with (1) proves
\[
\mathfrak M_{+}^{\mathrm{rm}}(\mathcal G)
\subsetneq
\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{lm}}(\mathcal G).
\]
The same argument also verifies the advertised general witness criterion: if a compatible finite \(\widetilde{\mathcal M}\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{lm}}(\mathcal G)\) has even one cell \((\widetilde v,\widetilde r)\) satisfying \(P_{\widetilde{\mathcal M}}(\widetilde v,\widetilde r)=0\), then the strict-positivity clause directly implies \(\widetilde{\mathcal M}\notin\mathfrak M_{+}^{\mathrm{rm}}(\mathcal G)\), so it is a witness to properness.

Finally, Definition \texttt{def:causal-query} gives on every ambient model \(\mathcal M\) the causal law
\[
Q_a^{\mathcal M}(y)
=P_{\mathcal M}\bigl(Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(A=a)\bigr)
\]
and the score-coded contrast
\[
\tau_{s_Y}(\mathcal M)
=\sum_{y\in\mathcal X_Y}s_Y(y)
\left\{Q_{a_1}^{\mathcal M}(y)-Q_{a_0}^{\mathcal M}(y)\right\}.
\tag{9}
\]
For each \(\mathcal M^{+}\in\mathfrak M_{+}^{\mathrm{rm}}(\mathcal G)\), inclusion (1) places \(\mathcal M^{+}\) in the domain of these ambient causal maps.  Evaluating the same formulas at \(\mathcal M^{+}\) gives exactly \(Q_a^{\mathcal M^{+}}\) and \(\tau_{s_Y}(\mathcal M^{+})\).  They are therefore the restrictions of the published natural interventional law and its score-coded NATE contrast to \(\mathfrak M_{+}^{\mathrm{rm}}(\mathcal G)\).  This is a restriction of causal targets; no equality with an observed-law functional has been assumed or defined in this proposition.

statements.statement: Suppose \(\operatorname{Swap}_{\kappa}(u,v)\) holds and both composite colored fixings are legal. After erasing the ordered provenance list \(\Lambda\), the two resulting states have the same CADMG, fixed set, context, normalized kernel, and observed-law provenance. Their two appended trace suffixes are respectively \(\bigl((\lambda_u,\pi),(\lambda_v,\Phi_u^{\lambda_u}\pi)\bigr)\) and \(\bigl((\lambda_v,\pi),(\lambda_u,\Phi_v^{\lambda_v}\pi)\bigr)\); hence the definition does not imply equality of the full trace states up to permutation. Branches may be merged only after replaying the two licenses in a fixed canonical order from their common pre-swap state.
statements.justification: A local confluence theorem is the algebraic invariant that makes a colored reachable kernel independent of arbitrary implementation order.
statements.gap: Richardson et al. prove adjacent-swap invariance inside one CADMG and kernel domain; they do not transport missingness licenses or pre-restriction provenance.
statements.consumer: The memoized identification procedure can merge equivalent fixing branches without deleting the Figure 3(b) pre-selection trace.
statements.proof_tex:
Let \(E\) erase only the ordered provenance list \(\Lambda\) from a trace-aware state.  Write the initial state as
\[
\kappa=(\mathcal H,F,c,q,\pi,\Lambda).
\tag{1}
\]
The premise that both colored composites are legal supplies fixability at each intermediate CADMG, validity of both licenses, and support of both denominator traces.  In addition, \(\text{ass:strict-positivity}\) makes every conditional kernel appearing in a legal fixing strictly positive on its stated support.  Thus every division below is defined.

Apply \(\text{lem:ordinary-adjacent-fixing-commutation}\) to the CADMG \(\mathcal H\) and normalized kernel \(q\).  Its hypotheses are the two fixability clauses in \(\operatorname{Swap}_{\kappa}(u,v)\), together with the assumed legality of both composites.  It gives
\[
\left(E\Phi_v^{\lambda_v}\Phi_u^{\lambda_u}(\kappa)\right)_{\mathcal H,q}
=
\left(E\Phi_u^{\lambda_u}\Phi_v^{\lambda_v}(\kappa)\right)_{\mathcal H,q}.
\tag{2}
\]
In either order the fixed set is \(F\cup\{u,v\}\), because each fixing adds its vertex and never removes a fixed vertex.  Deleting arrowheads into \(u\) and into \(v\) commutes, and fixing does not alter the context assignment \(c\).  Hence the CADMG, fixed-set, and context components in the two erased states agree.

By \(\text{def:colored-fixing}\), the provenance expression \(\pi\) is transformed by exactly the same two supported conditional-kernel divisions as \(q\).  Equality (2), viewed as the equality obtained after those two divisions, therefore gives equality of the resulting rational observed-law functions after cancellation of their nonzero denominators.  Thus
\[
E\Phi_v^{\lambda_v}\Phi_u^{\lambda_u}(\kappa)
=
E\Phi_u^{\lambda_u}\Phi_v^{\lambda_v}(\kappa)
\tag{3}
\]
in every component retained by \(E\).

It remains to calculate the component erased by \(E\).  Starting from the provenance \(\pi\), the order \(u,v\) appends
\[
\bigl((\lambda_u,\pi),(\lambda_v,\Phi_u^{\lambda_u}\pi)\bigr),
\tag{4}
\]
whereas the order \(v,u\) appends
\[
\bigl((\lambda_v,\pi),(\lambda_u,\Phi_v^{\lambda_v}\pi)\bigr).
\tag{5}
\]
Equations (4)--(5) follow directly from the append rule in \(\text{def:colored-fixing}\).  Merely permuting the two list positions does not replace \(\Phi_u^{\lambda_u}\pi\) by \(\pi\), or \(\Phi_v^{\lambda_v}\pi\) by \(\pi\); hence the hypotheses do not imply equality of the full ordered trace states up to permutation.  Finally, both branches have the same pre-swap state (1) and the same two licenses.  Replaying those licenses from (1) in a fixed canonical order deterministically recomputes one of (4)--(5), while (3) proves equality of all non-list components.  Therefore a branch merge is sound only after that canonical replay, as claimed.

statements.statement: For every compatible \(P_{\mathrm{3b}}\), a legal trace on \(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{3b}}\) first derives \(P(Y\mid\operatorname{do}(A=a),R_W)\) and then applies \(\Sigma_{R_W=0}\), yielding \[P(Y\mid\operatorname{do}(A=a))=P(Y\mid\operatorname{do}(A=a),R_W=0)=P_{\mathrm{3b}}(Y\mid A=a,R_W=0).\] Hence the unique TCF partition cell containing \(P_{\mathrm{3b}}\) carries this functional. The closure generated by restricting to \(R_W=0\) before any fixing step contains no kernel with the pre-selection provenance needed for the first equality.
statements.justification: This is the minimal regression test showing that provenance is identifying information rather than bookkeeping.
statements.gap: De Aguas et al. display the functional in Figure 3(b), but no existing calculus represents its fix-before-select derivation as a reusable typed kernel.
statements.consumer: The ADHD medication and test-achievement analysis can recover the NATE when treatment assignment changes after a grade-5 pre-test is missing.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix a compatible model \(\mathcal M\) inducing \(P_{\mathrm{3b}}\). In \(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{3b}}\), \(R_W\) has only its private exogenous factor and its only directed child is \(A\). After replacing the equation for \(A\) by the constant \(a\), the structural evaluation of \(Y\) contains no factor appearing in the equation for \(R_W\). Mutual independence of the individual-edge and private factors therefore gives, for every supported \(r\),
\[
P_{\mathcal M}(Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(A=a),R_W=r)
=P_{\mathcal M}(Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(A=a)).
\tag{6}
\]

When \(R_W=0\), label semantics deletes \(W\to A\). The remaining treatment equation is a function of \(R_W,Z\), and the private factor of \(A\). The counterfactual \(Y(a)\) is a function of \(a\), the private factor of \(Y\), and the factors on \(W\leftrightarrow Y\) and \(R_Z\leftrightarrow Y\). The former inputs are independent of the latter inputs. Hence
\[
Y(a)\mathbin{\perp\!\!\!\perp}A\mid R_W=0.
\tag{7}
\]
SCM consistency and (7), followed by (6), give
\[
\begin{aligned}
P_{\mathrm{3b}}(Y=y\mid A=a,R_W=0)
&=P_{\mathcal M}(Y(a)=y\mid A=a,R_W=0)\\
&=P_{\mathcal M}(Y(a)=y\mid R_W=0)\\
&=P_{\mathcal M}(Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(A=a)).
\end{aligned}
\]
Strict positivity justifies both conditionings and divisions.

The licensed fixing step records the pre-selection provenance for the kernel in (6); \(\Sigma_{R_W=0}\) then restricts it and retains that record. Conversely, if restriction is the first operation, the initial trace list is empty and every later provenance expression is a function of the already selected kernel. By the constructions of \(\Phi\) and \(\Sigma\), no later operation inserts the absent unselected provenance, proving the closure claim. Finally, the displayed observed expression has the same value in every model of the fiber. By \(\text{lem:semialgebraic-fiber-dichotomy}\), the unique cell is therefore identifying and carries that value.

statements.statement: For every finite positive regular-maximal \(\mathcal G\) and every observed law \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\), the polynomial presentation is exactly the compatible lm-SCM fiber in both directions. First, for every \(\mathcal M\in\mathfrak F(\mathcal G,P_{\mathrm{obs}})\), finite support reduction of each mutually independent individual-edge and private latent factor produces \(\theta_{\mathcal M}\) such that \(\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}(\theta_{\mathcal M};P_{\mathrm{obs}})\), \(p_{v,r}(\theta_{\mathcal M})=P_{\mathcal M}(v,r)\), and \(q_{a,y}(\theta_{\mathcal M})=Q_a^{\mathcal M}(y)\) for every \((v,r,a,y)\). Conversely, every \(\theta\) satisfying \(\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}(\theta;P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) decodes, using the unique selected table and the product law \(\prod_h\rho_h\), to a model \(\mathcal M_{\theta}\in\mathfrak F(\mathcal G,P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) with the same full-data cells and \(Q_a^{\mathcal M_{\theta}}(y)=q_{a,y}(\theta)\).
statements.justification: This two-way theorem prevents the algebraic oracle from enlarging a sparse bidirected graph into an unrestricted district-latent model.
statements.gap: Duarte et al. polynomialize finite response functions, but the required equality here is with the published lm-SCM fiber under individual bidirected-edge factorization and exact label deletions.
statements.consumer: Every soundness, completeness, and small-graph QE certificate can be interpreted as a claim about the published semi-Markovian model rather than a relaxation.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) and first take \(\mathcal M\in\mathfrak F(\mathcal G,P_{\mathrm{obs}})\). By \(\text{def:observational-fiber}\) and \(\text{def:positive-rm-class}\), \(\mathcal M\) has finite endogenous alphabets, its full law is strictly positive, and its exogenous variables consist of mutually independent individual-edge and private factors. Put
\[
L_{\mathcal G}=\left|\mathcal X_{\mathcal V}\times\mathcal X_{\mathcal R}\right|,
\qquad
K_{\mathrm{ub}}(\mathcal G)=L_{\mathcal G}+|\mathcal X_A|(|\mathcal X_Y|-1).
\tag{1}
\]
Applying \(\text{lem:finite-factor-support-reduction}\) sequentially to the finitely many factors yields a label-compatible deterministic response representation in which each factor has support at most \(K_{\mathrm{ub}}(\mathcal G)\), mutual independence is preserved, and simultaneously
\[
P(V=v,R=r)=P_{\mathcal M}(v,r),
\qquad
P(Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(A=a))=Q_a^{\mathcal M}(y)
\tag{2}
\]
for all \((v,r,a,y)\). The support lemma obtains (1) from the affine-dimension bound \((L_{\mathcal G}-1)+|\mathcal X_A|(|\mathcal X_Y|-1)\); no lower bound or sharpness assertion is used.

Pad a factor having fewer than \(K_{\mathrm{ub}}(\mathcal G)\) supported values by zero-weight states. Let \(\rho_{h,k}\) be the resulting marginal weights. The support reduction preserves the original structural equations on all positive-weight states, and \(\text{ass:label-semantics}\) makes their restricted tables an element \(g_*\in\mathcal T_{\mathcal G}\). Set
\[
\gamma_{g_*}=1,
\qquad
\gamma_g=0\quad(g\neq g_*).
\tag{3}
\]
Then
\[
\gamma_g^2-\gamma_g=0,
\qquad
\sum_g\gamma_g=1,
\qquad
\rho_{h,k}\geq0,
\qquad
\sum_{k=1}^{K_{\mathrm{ub}}(\mathcal G)}\rho_{h,k}=1.
\tag{4}
\]
By the product independence in \(\text{ass:semimarkovian}\), deterministic evaluation of the response tables gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
p_{v,r}(\theta_{\mathcal M})
&=\sum_u\mathbf 1\{g_*(u)=(v,r)\}\prod_h\rho_{h,u_h}
=P_{\mathcal M}(v,r),\\
q_{a,y}(\theta_{\mathcal M})
&=Q_a^{\mathcal M}(y).
\end{aligned}
\tag{5}
\]
The second equality uses (2) and \(\text{def:causal-query}\). Proxy consistency and the first equality in (5) imply
\[
p_o(\theta_{\mathcal M})
=\sum_{(v,r):\operatorname{proxy}(v,r)=o}P_{\mathcal M}(v,r)
=P_{\mathrm{obs}}(o).
\tag{6}
\]
Strict positivity in \(\text{def:positive-rm-class}\) gives \(p_{v,r}(\theta_{\mathcal M})>0\) for every full cell. Equations (3)--(6) are exactly the conjuncts of \(\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}(\theta_{\mathcal M};P_{\mathrm{obs}})\), proving the forward direction.

Conversely, suppose \(\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}(\theta;P_{\mathrm{obs}})\). Over \(\mathbb R\), each equation \(\gamma_g^2-\gamma_g=0\) implies \(\gamma_g\in\{0,1\}\). Together with \(\sum_g\gamma_g=1\), this yields a unique \(g_*\) satisfying \(\gamma_{g_*}=1\). For each \(h\in\mathcal J\), let \(U_h\) have law
\[
P(U_h=k)=\rho_{h,k},
\qquad 1\leq k\leq K_{\mathrm{ub}}(\mathcal G),
\tag{7}
\]
and construct these finitely many factors independently. Use \(g_*\) as the structural-table tuple. Since \(g_*\in\mathcal T_{\mathcal G}\), the equations respect the directed parents and every table identification imposed by a label. Thus \(\text{def:published-lm-class}\), \(\text{ass:semimarkovian}\), \(\text{ass:label-semantics}\), and \(\text{ass:proxy-consistency}\) show that the decoded object \(\mathcal M_\theta\) is an lm-SCM inducing \(\mathcal G\). Its finite response expansion is
\[
P_{\mathcal M_\theta}(v,r)
=\sum_u\mathbf 1\{g_*(u)=(v,r)\}\prod_h\rho_{h,u_h}
=p_{v,r}(\theta)>0.
\tag{8}
\]
The observed-cell equalities in \(\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}\), proxy consistency, and (8) give
\[
P_{\mathcal M_\theta}(\mathcal O=o)=p_o(\theta)=P_{\mathrm{obs}}(o).
\tag{9}
\]
Regularity and maximality are properties of the fixed input graph, and (8) supplies strict positivity. Hence (9) and \(\text{def:observational-fiber}\) imply \(\mathcal M_\theta\in\mathfrak F(\mathcal G,P_{\mathrm{obs}})\). Finally, replacing the equation for \(A\) by the constant \(a\) in the same product expansion gives
\[
Q_a^{\mathcal M_\theta}(y)=q_{a,y}(\theta).
\tag{10}
\]
Equations (1)--(10) prove both directions without replacing the graph's individual-edge factorization by an unrestricted district latent.

statements.statement: For every identifying cell \(\psi_j(\mathbf p)\in\mathscr P_{\mathcal G,A,Y}\), every compatible law \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) satisfying \(\psi_j((P_{\mathrm{obs}}(o))_o)\), every \(\mathcal M\in\mathfrak F(\mathcal G,P_{\mathrm{obs}})\), every \(a\in\mathcal X_A\), and every \(y\in\mathcal X_Y\), the cell's functional satisfies \[f_{a,j}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)=Q_a^{\mathcal M}(y).\] Consequently, \(\sum_y s_Y(y)\{f_{a_1,j}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)-f_{a_0,j}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)\}=\tau_{s_Y}\) throughout that fiber. This is a mathematical specialization statement and does not require a finite encoding of the population coordinates.
statements.justification: Every returned expression must be valid for the entire compatible positive lm-SCM class, not merely for the response-function oracle used in testing.
statements.gap: Tikka et al. prove soundness for CSI-calculus search and Bhattacharya et al. justify missing-law fixing, but neither result composes the two operations with retained proxy-trace provenance.
statements.consumer: Graphical software can expose the returned NATE value as a population estimand without a hidden restrict-first assumption.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix an identifying cell \(\psi_j\), a compatible law \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) whose observed-cell vector \(\mathbf p_{\mathrm{obs}}=(P_{\mathrm{obs}}(o))_o\) satisfies \(\psi_j\), a model \(\mathcal M\in\mathfrak F(\mathcal G,P_{\mathrm{obs}})\), and a coordinate \((a,y)\in\mathcal X_A\times\mathcal X_Y\).  By the forward direction of \(\text{thm:response-fiber-equivalence}\), there is a response vector \(\theta_{\mathcal M}\) such that
\[
\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}(\theta_{\mathcal M};\mathbf p_{\mathrm{obs}}),
\qquad
q_{a,y}(\theta_{\mathcal M})=Q_a^{\mathcal M}(y).
\tag{1}
\]
The first relation includes strict positivity of every full-data cell polynomial, so every trace division admitted by \(\text{def:tcf-procedure}\) is evaluated only after its nonzero denominator has been verified.

Because \(\psi_j\) is identifying, \(\mathsf I_{a,y}\) is true throughout it.  By \(\text{def:terminal-qe-test}\), at \(\mathbf p_{\mathrm{obs}}\) this says
\[
\neg\exists\theta^0\,\exists\theta^1
\left[
\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}(\theta^0;\mathbf p_{\mathrm{obs}})
\wedge
\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}(\theta^1;\mathbf p_{\mathrm{obs}})
\wedge
q_{a,y}(\theta^0)\neq q_{a,y}(\theta^1)
\right].
\tag{2}
\]
Thus all compatible response vectors have a common \(q_{a,y}\)-value.  Since (1) supplies at least one such vector, the relation
\[
\mathsf V_{a,y}(\mathbf p_{\mathrm{obs}},z)
\Longleftrightarrow
\exists\theta\,[\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}(\theta;\mathbf p_{\mathrm{obs}})\wedge z=q_{a,y}(\theta)]
\tag{3}
\]
has exactly one real solution, say \(z_*\).

There are two output cases.  If no rational trace annotation is certified on the whole cell, \(\text{def:tcf-procedure}\) stores (3), so by definition of the cellwise functional
\[
f_{a,j}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)=z_*.
\tag{4}
\]
If the compiler stores a rational trace \(r(\mathbf p)=N(\mathbf p)/D(\mathbf p)\), its whole-cell verification proves
\[
D(\mathbf p_{\mathrm{obs}})\neq0,
\qquad
D(\mathbf p_{\mathrm{obs}})z_*=N(\mathbf p_{\mathrm{obs}}).
\tag{5}
\]
The first equality licenses division, and the second then gives (4) in this case as well.  Combining (1), (3), and (4) yields
\[
f_{a,j}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)
=z_*
=q_{a,y}(\theta_{\mathcal M})
=Q_a^{\mathcal M}(y).
\tag{6}
\]
This argument takes place in the ordered field \(\mathbb R\); it uses no finite representation of the coordinates of \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\).

Apply (6) at \(a=a_1\) and \(a=a_0\), multiply the equality for each \(y\) by the supplied score \(s_Y(y)\), subtract, and sum over the finite alphabet \(\mathcal X_Y\).  By \(\text{def:causal-query}\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{y\in\mathcal X_Y}s_Y(y)
\{f_{a_1,j}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)-f_{a_0,j}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)\}
&=\sum_{y\in\mathcal X_Y}s_Y(y)
\{Q_{a_1}^{\mathcal M}(y)-Q_{a_0}^{\mathcal M}(y)\}\\
&=\tau_{s_Y}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{7}
\]
This proves both assertions.

statements.statement:
Let the quantities in \(\text{def:termination-budget}\) be fixed. For every finite \(\mathcal G\) and finite alphabets, the expression-discovery phase of \(\operatorname{TCF}(\mathcal G,A,Y,P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) visits at most
\[
B_{\mathrm{state}}=2^n c\sum_{j=0}^{2n}\bigl\{2^{n+1}+n(\ell+1)+c+1\bigr\}^j
\]
literal complete trace states \(\kappa=(\mathcal H,F,c,q,\pi,\Lambda)\), counting every fixing-selection interleaving and provenance-bearing history. Independently of those traces, the single base feasibility/coordinate-constancy CAD constructs \(\mathscr P_{\mathcal G,A,Y}\) within \(C_{\mathrm{base}}=\operatorname{CAD}(p,s)\) projection, root-isolation, sign-evaluation steps, and output cells. At most
\[
N_{\mathrm{check}}=|\mathcal X_A||\mathcal X_Y|B_{\mathrm{state}}C_{\mathrm{base}}
\]
whole-cell candidate-equality sentences are subsequently decided, and the total work is bounded by
\[
B_{\mathrm{tot}}=
B_{\mathrm{state}}+C_{\mathrm{base}}
+N_{\mathrm{check}}\operatorname{CAD}(p+1,s).
\]
Given \(\operatorname{Exact}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\), cell selection and Thom-encoded value or witness extraction over the real closure of the ordered field generated by \(\mathbf p\) terminate after finitely many exact sign decisions. No point computation is claimed for arbitrary unencoded population reals, and no polynomial-time claim is made.
statements.justification: The finite guarantee counts complete trace histories, one trace-independent base CAD, and every post-partition rational-annotation validation.
statements.gap: Prior searches do not expose the separation between response-fiber partition construction and trace-derived expression discovery.
statements.consumer: Small-graph audits can compare canonical cells with exact response elimination and separately check every Figure 3(b)-style trace annotation.
statements.proof_tex:
For a trace state \(\kappa\), let \(r(\kappa)\) be the number of random vertices in its current CADMG, and let \(d(c)\) be the number of missingness indicators assigned by its partial context.  Define
\[
\mu(\kappa)=r(\kappa)+|\mathcal R|-d(c).
\tag{1}
\]
This is a nonnegative integer.  Initially \(r(\kappa)\leq n\) and \(|\mathcal R|-d(c)\leq n\), so \(\mu(\kappa)\leq2n\).  Under \(\text{def:tcf-procedure}\), a strict ancestral marginalization, restriction to a proper district child, or licensed fixing reduces the random-vertex set by at least one.  A delayed selection strictly extends \(c\), and hence increases \(d(c)\) by at least one.  No permitted recursive transition increases either summand in (1).  Therefore every recursive operation word has length at most
\[
2n.
\tag{2}
\]

There are at most \(2^n\) observed margins.  For each indicator \(R_Z\), a partial context either leaves it unassigned or assigns one of \(|\mathcal X_{R_Z}|\) values; therefore the number of partial contexts is exactly bounded by
\[
c=\prod_{R_Z\in\mathcal R}(|\mathcal X_{R_Z}|+1).
\tag{3}
\]
Consequently there are at most \(2^n c\) initial traces.  From any state, each of the two strict subset operations has at most \(2^n\) choices, fixing has at most \(n(\ell+1)\) vertex-license choices, selection has at most \(c\) strict extensions, and one further symbol records termination.  Hence the operation alphabet has size at most
\[
L_{\mathrm{op}}=2^{n+1}+n(\ell+1)+c+1.
\tag{4}
\]
For a fixed initial trace and operation word, all components \((\mathcal H,F,c,q,\pi,\Lambda)\) are prescribed by the update rules.  From (2)--(4), the number of literal complete states visited is at most
\[
2^n c\sum_{j=0}^{2n}L_{\mathrm{op}}^j
=B_{\mathrm{state}}.
\tag{5}
\]
This count keeps every fixing-selection interleaving and every ordered provenance list.  By \(\text{lem:colored-adjacent-swap}\), ordinary kernel commutation alone does not identify unequal trace suffixes.  The optional optimization in \(\text{def:tcf-procedure}\) merges branches only after canonical replay and literal equality of the full tuple, so it can only decrease the bound (5).

The response-fiber feasibility and all coordinate-constancy formulas are formed once, independently of the traces.  A doubled constancy formula uses at most \(2\{g+hK_{\mathrm{ub}}(\mathcal G)\}\) response coordinates, and the free observed vector contributes \(|\mathcal X_{\mathcal O}|\) coordinates.  Thus the base input has at most
\[
p=2\{g+hK_{\mathrm{ub}}(\mathcal G)\}+|\mathcal X_{\mathcal O}|
\tag{6}
\]
variables.  Its complete binary encoding length is at most \(s\) by \(\text{def:termination-budget}\).  By the definition of the fixed finite CAD step bound \(\operatorname{CAD}(m,b)\), the single base call therefore terminates within
\[
C_{\mathrm{base}}=\operatorname{CAD}(p,s)
\tag{7}
\]
projection, real-root-isolation, and sign-evaluation steps and output cells.  In particular, the trace-independent partition has at most \(C_{\mathrm{base}}\) cells.

Each visited trace offers at most one candidate expression for each \((a,y)\) and each base cell.  Equations (5) and (7) therefore give at most
\[
N_{\mathrm{check}}
=|\mathcal X_A||\mathcal X_Y|B_{\mathrm{state}}C_{\mathrm{base}}
\tag{8}
\]
whole-cell candidate-equality tests.  After supported denominators are cleared, such a sentence contains one response vector, the scalar \(z\), and \(\mathbf p\).  It consequently has at most \(p+1\) variables; its complete encoding length is at most \(s\) by the definition of that size parameter.  Each test is thus decided within \(\operatorname{CAD}(p+1,s)\) steps.  Summing the trace visits, the one base CAD, and all annotation tests yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
B_{\mathrm{state}}+C_{\mathrm{base}}
+N_{\mathrm{check}}\operatorname{CAD}(p+1,s)
&=B_{\mathrm{tot}}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{9}
\]

Finally, the completed partition and its annotations mention only finitely many integer-polynomial signs.  Under \(\operatorname{Exact}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\), rational cells are evaluated by exact rational arithmetic, algebraic cells by the supplied square-free polynomials and isolating intervals, and general exact-real cells by the supplied sign oracle.  Hence the unique cell is selected after finitely many sign decisions.  The finite root-isolation output supplies the stated Thom encodings over the real closure of the ordered field generated by \(\mathbf p\).  These specialization operations terminate separately from (9).  Nothing in the argument defines computation on an unencoded population real or bounds (9) by a polynomial.

statements.statement:
For every finite positive regular-maximal \(\mathcal G\), every exact specialization \(\operatorname{Exact}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\), and every negative partition-cell sample \(\omega=(a,y,\theta^0,\theta^1)\) satisfying \(\mathsf W_j\), let \(\mathcal T\) be any finite retained operation history accompanying the terminal package. Then \(\operatorname{Compile}_{\mathrm{col}}\) terminates. It returns either \(\operatorname{found}(\kappa_*,D,D')\), where the displayed triple passes every conjunct of the tested predicate \(\Delta(\omega,\mathcal T)\), or \(\operatorname{exhausted}\), which means that no enumerated triple passes those conjuncts. Independently of this diagnostic tag, the decoded models satisfy
\[
\mathcal M_0,\mathcal M_1\in\mathfrak F(\mathcal G,P_{\mathrm{obs}}),
\qquad
P_{\mathcal M_0}(\mathcal O)=P_{\mathcal M_1}(\mathcal O)=P_{\mathrm{obs}},
\qquad
Q_a^{\mathcal M_0}(y)\neq Q_a^{\mathcal M_1}(y).
\]
Both models are strictly positive and retain the product over the individual bidirected-edge and private latent factors. No colored-hedge membership, forest realization, or alignment between the sample and a graphwise recursion failure is asserted.
statements.justification: The theorem turns an exact negative cell into an auditable strictly positive same-observed, different-query model pair and gives a terminating optional trace diagnostic.
statements.gap: The frozen core proves pointwise algebraic nonidentification but supplies no graph-only invariant that forces colored-hedge existence or aligns an arbitrary algebraic witness with a failed recursion branch.
statements.consumer: A negative exact-law decision yields two finite edge-factorized lm-SCMs whose observed and interventional polynomials can be checked directly.
statements.proof_tex:
Because \(\omega\) satisfies \(\mathsf W_j\), the negative-cell relation in \(\text{def:terminal-qe-test}\) and \(\text{def:symbolic-observed-partition}\) gives
\[
\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}(\theta^i;P_{\mathrm{obs}})
\quad(i=0,1),
\qquad
q_{a,y}(\theta^0)\neq q_{a,y}(\theta^1).
\tag{1}
\]
Applying \(\text{lem:negative-cell-model-pair}\) to (1) yields
\[
\mathcal M_i\in\mathfrak F(\mathcal G,P_{\mathrm{obs}}),
\qquad
P_{\mathcal M_i}(\mathcal O)=P_{\mathrm{obs}},
\qquad
Q_a^{\mathcal M_i}(y)=q_{a,y}(\theta^i)
\quad(i=0,1).
\tag{2}
\]
That lemma also proves that each decoded latent law is the product over the individual bidirected-edge and private factors and that every full-data cell is strictly positive. Substituting the last equalities in (2) into the inequality in (1) gives
\[
Q_a^{\mathcal M_0}(y)\neq Q_a^{\mathcal M_1}(y).
\tag{3}
\]

It remains to prove termination and the meaning of the diagnostic tag. The graph and \(\mathcal T\) are finite by hypothesis, so they have finitely many prefixes and finitely many vertex, district, ancestor, and edge-color candidates at each prefix. Every purely graphical conjunct is decidable by finite graph inspection. The stored traces are rational expressions in observed cells and response coordinates. Each denominator tested by the corrected \(\text{def:certificate-compiler}\) is supported on its pre-restriction trace. It is nonzero because (1) contains strict positivity of every full-data cell, and every required marginal or selected cell is a finite sum of such positive cells. Clearing the finite product of these nonzero denominators turns every trace equality or nonzero test into a polynomial sign test without changing its truth value.

By the corrected \(\text{def:exact-observed-specialization}\), the coordinates of \(\theta^0,\theta^1\) have Thom encodings over the real closure of the ordered field generated by \(\mathbf p\). Signed-subresultant evaluation at such an encoding reduces every required comparison to finitely many signs of integer polynomials at \(\mathbf p\), and \(\operatorname{Exact}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) decides those signs. Hence each candidate test terminates. The deterministic finite enumeration in \(\text{def:certificate-compiler}\) therefore either returns the first candidate passing every conjunct or exhausts all candidates. In both branches its model components are exactly those in (2), so (2)--(3) prove all affirmative model claims. Nothing in this argument infers a colored hedge or forest realization from a diagnostic record.

statements.statement:
For a finite positive regular-maximal \(\mathcal G\) and supplied \(A,Y\), the trace-independent base phase of \(\operatorname{TCF}\) constructs a finite semialgebraic partition
\[
\mathscr P_{\mathcal G,A,Y}
\quad\text{of}\quad
\{\mathbf p:\exists\theta\,\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}(\theta;\mathbf p)\},
\]
and the colored trace phase only annotates those fixed cells by expressions verified on the whole cell. For every compatible finite/full-positive \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\), every \(a\in\mathcal X_A\), and every \(y\in\mathcal X_Y\), its unique cell carries \(f_{a,j}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)\) if and only if \(\mathcal M\mapsto Q_a^{\mathcal M}(y)\) is constant on \(\mathfrak F(\mathcal G,P_{\mathrm{obs}})\); in that case
\[
f_{a,j}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)=Q_a^{\mathcal M}(y)
\quad\text{for every }\mathcal M\in\mathfrak F(\mathcal G,P_{\mathrm{obs}}).
\]
If the coordinate is not constant, the cell carries \(\mathsf W_j\), and even without \(\operatorname{Exact}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) there exist strictly positive individual-edge-factorized models \(\mathcal M_0,\mathcal M_1\in\mathfrak F(\mathcal G,P_{\mathrm{obs}})\subseteq\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{lm}}(\mathcal G)\) with the same observed proxy law and \(Q_a^{\mathcal M_0}(y)\neq Q_a^{\mathcal M_1}(y)\). Under \(\operatorname{Exact}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\), the procedure additionally extracts a represented witness pair, and \(\operatorname{Compile}_{\mathrm{col}}\) terminates with either a checked divergence record or an exhaustion tag. If every coordinate is constant for both \(a_0\) and \(a_1\), then the observed-law functional identifies the causal contrast on the finite/full-positive fiber:
\[
\tau_{s_Y}
=\sum_{y\in\mathcal X_Y}s_Y(y)
\{f_{a_1,j}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)-f_{a_0,j}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)\}.
\]
This is pointwise semialgebraic completeness for the finite/full-positive subclass, together with exact-free ambient nonidentification from every negative cell; it makes no graphwise colored-hedge completeness claim.
statements.justification: The flagship theorem gives an explicit observed-law map on constant finite fibers and a positive same-observed obstruction on nonconstant fibers.
statements.gap: Ambient positive identification and a colored-hedge failure converse remain outside the theorem; only negative results transfer upward.
statements.consumer: For the ADHD medication/test-achievement FATE and NATE analysis, each requested coordinate is either recovered or accompanied by a same-observed countermodel pair, with exactness required only for represented extraction.
statements.proof_tex:
Let
\[
\mathcal P_{\mathrm{feas}}
=\{\mathbf p:\exists\theta\,\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}(\theta;\mathbf p)\}.
\tag{1}
\]
By \(\text{thm:tcf-termination}\), the trace-independent base construction and the subsequent finite annotation phase terminate.  By \(\text{lem:semialgebraic-fiber-dichotomy}\), their base formulas form a finite pairwise-disjoint semialgebraic partition of (1).  The construction in \(\text{def:tcf-procedure}\) fixes these base cells before trace enumeration and permits a colored trace only to annotate a cell after the displayed whole-cell implication has been verified.  Thus the trace phase neither splits nor merges the partition.

Let \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) be compatible with the finite, strictly full-positive class.  The fiber is nonempty by compatibility.  For any \(\mathcal M\in\mathfrak F(\mathcal G,P_{\mathrm{obs}})\), the forward direction of \(\text{thm:response-fiber-equivalence}\) supplies \(\theta_{\mathcal M}\) with
\[
\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}(\theta_{\mathcal M};P_{\mathrm{obs}}).
\tag{2}
\]
Hence the observed-cell vector belongs to (1) and lies in a unique partition cell \(\psi_j\).

Fix \((a,y)\).  Unfolding \(\text{def:terminal-qe-test}\) gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathsf I_{a,y}(\mathcal G;P_{\mathrm{obs}})
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
&\neg\exists\theta^0\,\exists\theta^1
\bigl[
\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}(\theta^0;P_{\mathrm{obs}})
\wedge\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}(\theta^1;P_{\mathrm{obs}})\\
&\hspace{35mm}\wedge q_{a,y}(\theta^0)\neq q_{a,y}(\theta^1)
\bigr].
\end{aligned}
\tag{3}
\]
Thus (3) holds exactly when \(q_{a,y}\) is constant on the polynomial fiber.  The two directions of \(\text{thm:response-fiber-equivalence}\) map that fiber onto \(\mathfrak F(\mathcal G,P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) and preserve the coordinate according to
\[
q_{a,y}(\theta)=Q_a^{\mathcal M_\theta}(y),
\qquad
q_{a,y}(\theta_{\mathcal M})=Q_a^{\mathcal M}(y).
\tag{4}
\]
Equations (3)--(4) prove
\[
\mathsf I_{a,y}(\mathcal G;P_{\mathrm{obs}})
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\mathcal M\longmapsto Q_a^{\mathcal M}(y)
\text{ is constant on }\mathfrak F(\mathcal G,P_{\mathrm{obs}}).
\tag{5}
\]

Suppose first that (5) holds.  The value relation \(\mathsf V_{a,y}(P_{\mathrm{obs}},z)\) is nonempty by (2) and single-valued by (3).  If no trace annotation passes, the cell stores this unique-value graph.  If a rational expression \(N/D\) passes, its verified whole-cell implication gives \(D(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\neq0\) and \(D(P_{\mathrm{obs}})z=N(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) at the unique value.  In either case the cell carries a well-defined \(f_{a,j}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)\).  Applying \(\text{thm:tcf-soundness}\) gives the explicit identifying equality
\[
f_{a,j}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)=Q_a^{\mathcal M}(y)
\quad
\text{for every }\mathcal M\in\mathfrak F(\mathcal G,P_{\mathrm{obs}}).
\tag{6}
\]
Conversely, a cell can carry such an identifying functional only if the right side of (6) is the same for all models in the fiber.  This proves the stated if-and-only-if characterization.

Suppose instead that (5) fails.  Then the unique cell carries the unnegated doubled relation \(\mathsf W_j\) by \(\text{lem:semialgebraic-fiber-dichotomy}\).  Its satisfiability is a statement over \(\mathbb R\) and does not require an effective encoding of its solutions.  Applying \(\text{prop:ambient-nonrecovery-transfer}\) gives strictly positive, individual-edge-factorized models
\[
\mathcal M_0,\mathcal M_1
\in\mathfrak F(\mathcal G,P_{\mathrm{obs}})
\subseteq\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{lm}}(\mathcal G),
\tag{7}
\]
such that
\[
P_{\mathcal M_0}(\mathcal O)
=P_{\mathcal M_1}(\mathcal O)
=P_{\mathrm{obs}},
\qquad
Q_a^{\mathcal M_0}(y)\neq Q_a^{\mathcal M_1}(y).
\tag{8}
\]
Equations (7)--(8) are the exact-free obstruction in both the finite/full-positive fiber and, by inclusion, the published ambient class.

If \(\operatorname{Exact}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) is supplied, \(\text{def:exact-observed-specialization}\) selects the unique cell and represents a satisfying pair by Thom encodings over the real closure of the ordered field generated by \(\mathbf p\).  Choose any finite retained operation history \(\mathcal T\) accompanying the terminal package; its finiteness follows from \(\text{thm:tcf-termination}\).  Then \(\text{thm:qe-failure-compiler}\) decodes a pair satisfying (7)--(8) and terminates with either a checked divergence record or the exhaustion tag.  That theorem asserts no colored hedge, and none is used here.

Finally, assume every outcome coordinate is constant for both \(a_0\) and \(a_1\).  The outcome alphabet is finite by \(\text{ass:finite-alphabets}\), so coordinatewise substitution from (6) into \(\text{def:causal-query}\) is legitimate and gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\tau_{s_Y}
&=\sum_{y\in\mathcal X_Y}s_Y(y)
\{Q_{a_1}^{\mathcal M}(y)-Q_{a_0}^{\mathcal M}(y)\}\\
&=\sum_{y\in\mathcal X_Y}s_Y(y)
\{f_{a_1,j}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)-f_{a_0,j}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)\}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{9}
\]
This proves the finite/full-positive pointwise completeness claim, its explicit observed-law identifying map, and its same-observed negative certificate, without enlarging the positive identification domain or asserting graphwise colored-hedge completeness.

statements.statement: For the worked member \(\mathcal G_\star=\mathcal G(\{C\},1)\), every compatible \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) satisfies \[Q_a(y)=\sum_{c}P_{\mathrm{obs}}(c)\sum_bP_{\mathrm{obs}}(b\mid a,c,R_W=0)\sum_{a'}P_{\mathrm{obs}}(y\mid b,a',c,R_W=0)P_{\mathrm{obs}}(a'\mid c,R_W=0)=f_a^\star(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y).\] The derivation first records \(P(Y\mid\operatorname{do}(A),R_W)\), then selects \(R_W=0\), uses \(B_1\) as the front-door set conditional on \(C\), and averages over the unselected \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}(C)\). No de Aguas Proposition 4 certificate exists: the edge \(A\leftrightarrow Y\) remains an open length-one path in every \(\mathcal H_r[\underline A]\), so condition \(\mathrm{(v)}\) fails for every \(K,H,\{L_r\}_r\). The root-control procedure is inapplicable because \(C\to R_W\), so its required context variable is not a causal root. The TCF partition places every compatible observed law on an identifying cell carrying \(f_a^\star\).
statements.justification: A fully specified member makes the strict-separation claim checkable edge by edge and formula by formula.
statements.gap: The published Figure 3(b) functional is covered by Proposition 4; adding endogenous indicator parentage and front-door confounding creates a concrete member outside both published certificates while retaining recovery.
statements.consumer: The member is the exact small-graph regression test for medication assignment driven by whether a pre-test is available and for a fully observed treatment-adherence mediator.
statements.proof_tex:
Apply \(\text{lem:eipfd-frontdoor-identification}\) with \(H=\{C\}\) and \(m=1\).  Its strict-positivity premise is inherited from \(\mathfrak M_{+}^{\mathrm{rm}}(\mathcal G_\star)\), so every conditional denominator in the displayed functional is positive.  The lemma gives, for every model in the observed-law fiber,
\[
\begin{aligned}
Q_a^{\mathcal M}(y)
&=\sum_{c\in\mathcal X_C}P_{\mathrm{obs}}(c)
\sum_{b\in\mathcal X_{B_1}}P_{\mathrm{obs}}(b\mid a,c,R_W=0)\\
&\qquad\times\sum_{a'\in\mathcal X_A}
P_{\mathrm{obs}}(y\mid b,a',c,R_W=0)
P_{\mathrm{obs}}(a'\mid c,R_W=0).
\end{aligned}
\tag{1}
\]
By \(\text{def:eipfd-star-functional}\), the right side of (1) is exactly \(f_a^\star(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)\).  The proof of the cited lemma first retains the interventional kernel conditional on \(R_W\), then invokes the label only in the selected context \(R_W=0\), performs the front-door adjustment through \(B_1\) conditional on \(C\), and finally uses the unselected marginal \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}(C)\).  This is the operation order stated in the proposition.

We next exclude a de Aguas certificate.  By \(\text{def:endogenous-proxy-frontdoor-class}\), \(A\leftrightarrow Y\) is present in \(\mathcal G_\star\).  Deleting directed arrows out of \(A\) does not delete a bidirected edge.  Hence, in every candidate graph \(\mathcal H_r[\underline A]\), the edge \(A\leftrightarrow Y\) is an open path of length one.  It has no nonendpoint that an admissible conditioning set could block.  Therefore the d-separation required by condition \(\mathrm{(v)}\) in \(\text{def:da4-certificate-functional}\) fails for every candidate \((K,H,\{L_r\}_r)\), and
\[
\operatorname{DA4}(\mathcal G_\star,A,Y)=\varnothing.
\tag{2}
\]
The graph also contains \(C\to R_W\).  Thus the label-context variable \(R_W\) is not parentless, so the observed-causal-root premise in \(\operatorname{RC}(\mathcal G_\star,A,Y)\) fails:
\[
\neg\operatorname{RC}(\mathcal G_\star,A,Y).
\tag{3}
\]

Finally, (1) is a functional only of \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\), and it equals the causal coordinate for every model in the fiber.  Hence that coordinate is constant on the fiber.  By \(\text{lem:semialgebraic-fiber-dichotomy}\), the unique TCF cell containing every compatible observed law is identifying for the coordinate.  By \(\text{thm:tcf-soundness}\), the value carried by that cell equals (1), namely \(f_a^\star(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)\).  Together with (2)--(3), this proves every assertion.

statements.statement: On the common finite, strictly positive regular-maximal labeled-missingness subclass, TCF is a strict class-relative extension of the de Aguas Proposition 4 criterion and an embedding of the Mokhtarian observed-root theorem. More precisely, for every finite positive regular-maximal \(\mathcal G\), compatible \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\), treatment value \(a\), outcome value \(y\), and \(\xi\in\operatorname{DA4}(\mathcal G,A,Y)\), the unique TCF cell \(\psi_j\in\mathscr P_{\mathcal G,A,Y}\) carries \[f_{a,j}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)=f^{\mathrm{DA4}}_{a,\xi}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y).\] Whenever \(\operatorname{RC}(\mathcal G,A,Y)\) holds, the same cell carries \(f_{a,j}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)=f_a^{\mathrm{RC}}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)\). The de Aguas containment is strict on \(\mathfrak G_{\mathrm{EIPFD}}\): for every \(\mathcal G(H,m)\) and every compatible \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\), \(\operatorname{DA4}(\mathcal G(H,m),A,Y)=\varnothing\), while the TCF cell carries \[\sum_hP_{\mathrm{obs}}(h)\sum_bP_{\mathrm{obs}}(b\mid a,h,R_W=0)\sum_{a'}P_{\mathrm{obs}}(y\mid b,a',h,R_W=0)P_{\mathrm{obs}}(a'\mid h,R_W=0),\] where \(b\) ranges over \(B_1\). The arrow \(C\to R_W\) shows that the observed-root premise is inapplicable to this family; it is not a strictness claim about the complete published root-control domain. For \(H=\{C\}\) and \(m=1\), the displayed functional is exactly \(f_a^\star(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)\) of \(\text{prop:eipfd-star-worked}\).
statements.justification: The theorem makes the comparison at the domain actually proved: a strict de Aguas criterion extension and a Mokhtarian root-control embedding on the common finite positive intersection.
statements.gap: No theorem here extends EIPFD identification to the categorical-or-continuous ambient class under only observed-data positivity.
statements.consumer: Applied users retain the published formula when its source conditions hold on the common subclass and obtain the delayed-selection front-door formula for the finite positive EIPFD family.
statements.proof_tex:
Let \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) be compatible with the finite, strictly positive regular-maximal class, so \(\mathfrak F(\mathcal G,P_{\mathrm{obs}})\neq\varnothing\).  Fix \((a,y)\), and let \(\psi_j\) be the unique TCF cell containing the observed-cell vector.

First take \(\xi\in\operatorname{DA4}(\mathcal G,A,Y)\).  The cited recovery result \(\text{lem:da4-recovery}\) gives, for every \(\mathcal M\) in the fiber,
\[
f^{\mathrm{DA4}}_{a,\xi}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)
=Q_a^{\mathcal M}(y).
\tag{1}
\]
Because the left side depends only on the observed law, the query coordinate is constant over the fiber.  The equivalence in \(\text{lem:semialgebraic-fiber-dichotomy}\) makes \(\psi_j\) identifying, and \(\text{thm:tcf-soundness}\) gives
\[
f_{a,j}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)=Q_a^{\mathcal M}(y).
\tag{2}
\]
Combining (1)--(2) proves
\[
f_{a,j}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)
=f^{\mathrm{DA4}}_{a,\xi}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y).
\tag{3}
\]

If instead \(\operatorname{RC}(\mathcal G,A,Y)\) holds, the cited result \(\text{lem:root-control-context-recovery}\) gives
\[
f_a^{\mathrm{RC}}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)=Q_a^{\mathcal M}(y)
