\quad\text{for every }\mathcal M\in\mathfrak F(\mathcal G,P_{\mathrm{obs}}).
\tag{4}
\]
The same constancy, dichotomy, and soundness argument now gives
\[
f_{a,j}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)=f_a^{\mathrm{RC}}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y).
\tag{5}
\]
This is an embedding on the common finite, full-positive domain; no implication beyond that common domain has been used.

To prove strictness of (3), fix \(\mathcal G(H,m)\in\mathfrak G_{\mathrm{EIPFD}}\).  The graph contains \(A\leftrightarrow Y\).  This edge remains an open length-one path after directed arrows out of \(A\) are deleted, and no admissible conditioning vertex lies on that path.  Thus condition \(\mathrm{(v)}\) in every proposed de Aguas certificate fails, so
\[
\operatorname{DA4}(\mathcal G(H,m),A,Y)=\varnothing.
\tag{6}
\]
On the other hand, \(\text{lem:eipfd-frontdoor-identification}\) gives for every model in the nonempty fiber
\[
\begin{aligned}
Q_a^{\mathcal M}(y)
&=\sum_hP_{\mathrm{obs}}(h)
\sum_{b\in\mathcal X_{B_1}}P_{\mathrm{obs}}(b\mid a,h,R_W=0)\\
&\qquad\times\sum_{a'\in\mathcal X_A}
P_{\mathrm{obs}}(y\mid b,a',h,R_W=0)
P_{\mathrm{obs}}(a'\mid h,R_W=0).
\end{aligned}
\tag{7}
\]
Strict full-data positivity implies positivity of every marginal conditioning event in (7), so every division is defined.  The right side is an observed-law functional; therefore the coordinate is constant on the fiber, and \(\text{lem:semialgebraic-fiber-dichotomy}\) plus \(\text{thm:tcf-soundness}\) shows that the TCF cell carries (7).  Equations (6)--(7) exhibit an entire TCF-identified family outside the de Aguas certificate domain, proving the asserted strict class-relative extension.

Finally, every member of this family contains \(C\to R_W\).  Thus \(R_W\) is not an observed causal root, and the premise of \(\operatorname{RC}\) is inapplicable.  This is only a failure of the root-control premise, not a strictness conclusion about its full published domain.  When \(H=\{C\}\) and \(m=1\), \(\text{prop:eipfd-star-worked}\) identifies (7) term by term with \(f_a^\star(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)\), completing the proof.

statements.statement: When \(\mathcal R=\varnothing\), \(\mathcal V^{\dagger}=\varnothing\), and the label set is empty, the color and context components are vacuous and every rational trace returned by the graphical part of TCF is the corresponding ordinary \(\operatorname{ID}\) fixing expression. If ordinary \(\operatorname{ID}\) returns a functional \(f_a^{\mathrm{ID}}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)\), then every compatible \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) lies on a TCF cell identifying that coordinate and carrying exactly \(f_a^{\mathrm{ID}}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)\). The semialgebraic pointwise partition may refine the graphwise ID dichotomy, so no converse failure or hedge-compiler claim is made here.
statements.justification: The no-missingness reduction is the mandatory sanity check for both positive and negative outputs.
statements.gap: This is a regression theorem rather than a novelty claim; it ensures that added colors do not alter classical identification.
statements.consumer: Existing ordinary-ID implementations obtain a checkable base case for the new procedure.
statements.proof_tex:
Assume \(\mathcal R=\varnothing\), \(\mathcal V^{\dagger}=\varnothing\), and the label set is empty.  There is then exactly one empty context, no selection transition, and no nontrivial label license.  The observed record is the substantive record.  Unfolding \(\text{def:trace-state}\) and \(\text{def:tcf-procedure}\), the only graphical transitions are ancestral marginalization, district decomposition, and uncolored fixing.  These are exactly the transitions of ordinary \(\operatorname{ID}\), and the extra context and color components remain vacuous.  Hence every rational graphical trace returned by TCF is syntactically the corresponding ordinary fixing expression.

Suppose ordinary \(\operatorname{ID}\) returns \(f_a^{\mathrm{ID}}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)\).  By the cited soundness theorem \(\text{lem:ordinary-id-soundness}\),
\[
Q_a^{\mathcal M}(y)=f_a^{\mathrm{ID}}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)
\quad\text{for every }\mathcal M\in\mathfrak F(\mathcal G,P_{\mathrm{obs}}).
\tag{1}
\]
The right side is fixed by the observed law, so the causal coordinate is constant on the fiber.  By \(\text{lem:semialgebraic-fiber-dichotomy}\), the unique TCF cell is identifying.  The ordinary trace is among the enumerated candidates, and its equality with the unique value is valid on every compatible point of the cell by (1); therefore the whole-cell annotation test in \(\text{def:tcf-procedure}\) accepts it.  Applying \(\text{thm:tcf-soundness}\) gives
\[
f_{a,j}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)
=Q_a^{\mathcal M}(y)
=f_a^{\mathrm{ID}}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y).
\tag{2}
\]
The semialgebraic test is pointwise in an observed law, whereas the ordinary ID graphwise dichotomy is uniform over compatible laws.  Equations (1)--(2) prove the asserted one-way reduction and do not entail the excluded converse.

statements.statement: Whenever \(\operatorname{RC}(\mathcal G,A,Y)\) holds and every context-specific graph is identifying, delayed restriction is unnecessary. For every compatible \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\), its unique TCF partition cell is identifying and, for every \(a,y\), carries exactly \(f_a^{\mathrm{RC}}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)\). No converse is asserted for identification at one exceptional observed law.
statements.justification: The reduction locates the new difficulty precisely in endogenous missingness and observed-proxy traces.
statements.gap: Mokhtarian et al. prove completeness for observed root controls; their proof does not cover endogenous indicators, proxy censoring, or fix-before-select traces.
statements.consumer: Users can retain the simpler context-by-context algorithm whenever its published root-control conditions hold.
statements.proof_tex:
Assume \(\operatorname{RC}(\mathcal G,A,Y)\) and that every context graph is identifying.  By \(\text{def:root-control-functional}\), every label-context variable is observed and parentless.  Consequently intervention on \(A\) does not alter the context law:
\[
P_{\mathcal M}(C=c\mid\operatorname{do}(A=a))=P_{\mathrm{obs}}(C=c).
\tag{1}
\]
The cited result \(\text{lem:root-control-context-recovery}\) supplies, in every context, a sound functional \(f^{\mathrm{ID}}_{a,c}\) and the aggregation identity
\[
\begin{aligned}
Q_a^{\mathcal M}(y)
&=\sum_cP_{\mathrm{obs}}(C=c)
f^{\mathrm{ID}}_{a,c}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)\\
&=f_a^{\mathrm{RC}}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)
\end{aligned}
\tag{2}
\]
for every \(\mathcal M\in\mathfrak F(\mathcal G,P_{\mathrm{obs}})\).  Positivity in the finite class ensures that every context retained in a conditional expression has supported denominators; zero-weight contexts, if any occur in the published aggregation notation, contribute zero and need no division.

Because the contexts are roots, their restriction may be performed before the context-specific ordinary ID steps: no pre-restriction parent mechanism or provenance is lost.  Thus delayed restriction adds no identifying information in this regime.  Moreover, the last expression in (2) is common to the entire observed-law fiber.  By \(\text{lem:semialgebraic-fiber-dichotomy}\), the unique TCF cell is identifying, and by \(\text{thm:tcf-soundness}\),
\[
f_{a,j}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)
=Q_a^{\mathcal M}(y)
=f_a^{\mathrm{RC}}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y).
\tag{3}
\]
The cited root-control theorem is a graphwise result, while TCF also tests constancy at a particular observed law.  Therefore (3) proves the stated reduction but supplies no converse for an exceptional law, exactly as claimed.

statements.statement: The universal binary-witness assertion is false, and the smallest substantive alphabet vector is not determined by the color and district structure of a colored hedge alone. There exist a finite regular-maximal graph \(\mathcal G\), a hedge in \(\operatorname{CH}(\mathcal G,A,Y)\), and a strictly positive compatible \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) for which two models in \(\mathfrak F(\mathcal G,P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) have different \(Q_a\), but no model matching \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) can make every substantive variable binary. More generally, an always-observed substantive coordinate requires at least the cardinality of its observed support, and a partially observed coordinate \(Z\) requires at least \(|\operatorname{supp}(Z^{\dagger}\mid R_Z=1)|\). Under strict positivity these lower bounds equal the declared substantive alphabet cardinalities.
statements.proof_tex:
We give an explicit finite counterexample and then prove the support assertions.

Let \(\mathcal V=\{A,Y,Z\}\), let \(\mathcal R=\varnothing\), let \(\mathcal X_A=\mathcal X_Y=\{0,1\}\), and let \(\mathcal X_Z=\{0,1,2\}\). Thus every substantive variable is always observed and \(\mathcal O=(A,Y,Z)\). Let \(\mathcal G\) have the directed edge \(A\to Y\), the bidirected edge \(A\leftrightarrow Y\), the isolated vertex \(Z\), and the empty label set. Its directed part is acyclic, as required by \(\mathrm{ass{:}acyclic}\). Because \(\mathcal R=\varnothing\), there is no missingness context in which a label could occur; consequently the empty label set is regular and maximal, as required by \(\mathrm{ass{:}regular}\) and \(\mathrm{ass{:}maximal}\). Assumptions \(\mathrm{ass{:}proxy\text{-}consistency}\) and \(\mathrm{ass{:}label\text{-}semantics}\) are vacuous for this graph.

Let \(\mathcal F\) be the \(C\)-forest induced by \(\{A,Y\}\), and let \(\mathcal F'\) be its subforest induced by \(\{Y\}\). Indeed, \(\mathcal F\) is bidirected-connected, \(A\) has the unique directed child \(Y\), and \(Y\) has no directed child, so its root set is \(\{Y\}\); \(\mathcal F'\) has the same root set. Moreover,
\[
 \mathcal F\cap\{A\}=\{A\},
 \qquad
 \mathcal F'\cap\{A\}=\varnothing.
\]
The common root \(Y\) is an ancestor of \(Y\) after intervention on \(A\), since a vertex is its own ancestor. Take the empty color assignment and the trace family consisting only of the empty trace. This trace family is prefix closed, and the licensing condition is vacuous because no color occurs. Hence, by \(\mathrm{def{:}colored\text{-}hedge}\),
\[
 H=(\mathcal F,\mathcal F',\varnothing,\{\varnothing\})
 \in \operatorname{CH}(\mathcal G,A,Y).
\]

We next construct two compatible models. Let \(U\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) be the exogenous factor shared by \(A\) and \(Y\). Independently, let \(E_A\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/4)\), let \(E_Y\) be uniform on \(\{1,\ldots,16\}\), and let \(E_Z\) be uniform on \(\{0,1,2\}\). Put
\[
 A=U\mathbin{\oplus}E_A,
 \qquad
 Z=E_Z,
 \qquad
 t_0=\frac14,
 \qquad
 t_1=-\frac14,
\]
where \(\oplus\) denotes addition modulo two and the Bernoulli parameter is the probability of value one. For \(i\in\{0,1\}\), define
\[
 k_i(u,a)
 =16\left[\frac12+t_i\left\{\mathbf 1(u=a)-\frac34\right\}\right],
\]
and in model \(\mathcal M_i\) set
\[
 Y=\mathbf 1\{E_Y\leq k_i(U,A)\}.
\]
These are deterministic finite response tables because the thresholds are integers: \(k_0(u,a)\) is \(9\) when \(u=a\) and \(5\) otherwise, whereas \(k_1(u,a)\) is \(7\) when \(u=a\) and \(11\) otherwise. For each model, the equation for \(A\) depends on the shared factor \(U\), while the equation for \(Y\) depends on both \(A\) and \(U\), because changing the truth value of \(u=a\) changes the threshold. Thus the directed edge \(A\to Y\) and the individual bidirected-edge factor for \(A\leftrightarrow Y\) are active, and no additional edge is introduced. The factors \(U,E_A,E_Y,E_Z\) are mutually independent, so \(\mathrm{ass{:}semimarkovian}\) holds. The empty label set imposes no further response-table restriction.

For positivity, define
\[
 \pi_i(u,a)=\frac{k_i(u,a)}{16}.
\]
The displayed threshold values give \(0<\pi_i(u,a)<1\) for every \(i,u,a\). Moreover, \(P(E_A=e)>0\) for both \(e\in\{0,1\}\). Therefore, for every \((a,y,z)\in\mathcal X_A\times\mathcal X_Y\times\mathcal X_Z\), independence and the structural equations give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 P_{\mathcal M_i}(A=a,Y=y,Z=z)
 &=\frac13\sum_{u=0}^1
 \frac12 P(E_A=a\mathbin{\oplus}u)
 \pi_i(u,a)^y\{1-\pi_i(u,a)\}^{1-y}\\
 &>0.
 \end{aligned}
\]
This verifies \(\mathrm{ass{:}strict\text{-}positivity}\) cell by cell. All alphabets are finite, as required by \(\mathrm{ass{:}finite\text{-}alphabets}\). The graph conditions established above and \(\mathrm{def{:}positive\text{-}rm\text{-}class}\) therefore imply
\[
 \mathcal M_0,\mathcal M_1
 \in\mathfrak M_{+}^{\mathrm{rm}}(\mathcal G).
\]

We now compute the observed laws. For either \(a\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
 P_{\mathcal M_i}(A=a)
 =\sum_{u=0}^1\frac12P(E_A=a\mathbin{\oplus}u)
 =\frac12\left(\frac34+\frac14\right)
 =\frac12,
\]
and
\[
 P_{\mathcal M_i}(U=a,A=a)
 =P(U=a,E_A=0)
 =\frac12\cdot\frac34
 =\frac38.
\]
Division is legitimate because \(P_{\mathcal M_i}(A=a)=1/2>0\), and hence
\[
 P_{\mathcal M_i}(U=a\mid A=a)
 =\frac{3/8}{1/2}
 =\frac34.
\]
Using the response equation for \(Y\) and the conditional law of total probability,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 P_{\mathcal M_i}(Y=1\mid A=a)
 &=\sum_{u=0}^1
 \left[\frac12+t_i\left\{\mathbf 1(u=a)-\frac34\right\}\right]
 P_{\mathcal M_i}(U=u\mid A=a)\\
 &=\frac12+t_i\left\{P_{\mathcal M_i}(U=a\mid A=a)-\frac34\right\}\\
 &=\frac12.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Since \(Z=E_Z\) is independent and uniform, both models consequently induce
\[
 P_{\mathcal M_i}(A=a,Y=y,Z=z)
 =\frac12\cdot\frac12\cdot\frac13
 =\frac1{12}
\]
for every observed cell. Let \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) denote this common uniform, and hence strictly positive, observed law.

Under \(\operatorname{do}(A=a)\), the structural intervention in \(\mathrm{def{:}causal\text{-}query}\) replaces the equation for \(A\) by the constant \(a\) and leaves the exogenous distribution, in particular \(U\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\), unchanged. Therefore
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 Q_a^{\mathcal M_i}(1)
 &=\sum_{u=0}^1
 \left[\frac12+t_i\left\{\mathbf 1(u=a)-\frac34\right\}\right]P(U=u)\\
 &=\frac12+t_i\left(\frac12-\frac34\right)\\
 &=\frac12-\frac{t_i}{4}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
It follows that
\[
 Q_a^{\mathcal M_0}(1)=\frac7{16},
 \qquad
 Q_a^{\mathcal M_1}(1)=\frac9{16}.
\]
By \(\mathrm{def{:}observational\text{-}fiber}\), both models lie in \(\mathfrak F(\mathcal G,P_{\mathrm{obs}})\), but their interventional laws differ. Thus the displayed colored hedge has two strictly positive observationally equivalent witnesses with different \(Q_a\).

It remains to prove that no universal binary witness can match this observed law and to establish the general support claim. Let \(W\) be always observed and define
\[
 S_W=\{w:P_{\mathrm{obs}}(W=w)>0\}.
\]
In any model inducing \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\), the observed value of \(W\) is its substantive value, so
\[
 S_W\subseteq\mathcal X_W
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 |\mathcal X_W|\geq |S_W|.
\]
For a partially observed substantive coordinate \(W\), \(\mathrm{ass{:}proxy\text{-}consistency}\) gives \(W^{\dagger}=W\) on \(R_W=1\). The required conditioning event has positive probability under \(\mathrm{ass{:}strict\text{-}positivity}\): by \(\mathrm{ass{:}finite\text{-}alphabets}\), summing the finitely many positive full-data cells with \(R_W=1\) gives \(P_{\mathcal M}(R_W=1)>0\). Consequently
\[
 S_W^{\dagger}
 =\operatorname{supp}_{P_{\mathrm{obs}}}(W^{\dagger}\mid R_W=1)
 \subseteq\mathcal X_W,
\]
and hence
\[
 |\mathcal X_W|\geq |S_W^{\dagger}|.
\]

Under \(\mathrm{ass{:}strict\text{-}positivity}\), both inclusions are equalities at the level of supports. Indeed, for every \(w\in\mathcal X_W\), summing the positive full-data cells whose substantive coordinate is \(W=w\) yields
\[
 P_{\mathcal M}(W=w)>0
\]
when \(W\) is always observed. If \(W\) is partially observed, summing the positive full-data cells with \(W=w\) and \(R_W=1\) gives
\[
 P_{\mathcal M}(W=w,R_W=1)>0.
\]
By \(\mathrm{ass{:}proxy\text{-}consistency}\), this equals
\[
 P_{\mathrm{obs}}(W^{\dagger}=w,R_W=1)>0.
\]
Thus every declared substantive value occurs in the conditional proxy support. Conversely, proxy consistency permits no value outside \(\mathcal X_W\) on \(R_W=1\). We have therefore proved
\[
 |S_W|=|\mathcal X_W|
 \quad\text{for always-observed }W,
 \qquad
 |S_W^{\dagger}|=|\mathcal X_W|
 \quad\text{for partially observed }W.
\]

In the constructed common law, \(S_Z=\{0,1,2\}\). Hence every model matching \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) must satisfy \(|\mathcal X_Z|\geq3\), so no such model can make every substantive variable binary. This disproves the universal binary-witness assertion.

Finally, for an arbitrary integer \(m\geq2\), replace \(\mathcal X_Z\) by \(\{0,\ldots,m-1\}\) and take \(E_Z\) uniform on it, leaving the equations for \(A\) and \(Y\) unchanged. The same computation gives two strictly positive models with a common observed law and distinct query values. The forests \(\mathcal F'\subseteq\mathcal F\), their districts and roots, the empty coloring, and the trace family are unchanged because \(Z\) is isolated and belongs to neither forest. On the other hand, the observed support of \(Z\) has cardinality \(m\), so the support argument forces \(|\mathcal X_Z|\geq m\); the displayed construction attains equality. Thus the smallest required \(Z\)-alphabet coordinate is \(m\), while the colored hedge data are fixed. Since \(m\) is arbitrary, the smallest substantive alphabet vector is not determined by the color and district structure of a colored hedge alone. This proves every assertion of the theorem.

statements.statement:
Let \(\mathcal M\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{lm}}(\mathcal G)\) have finite endogenous alphabets and the mutually independent individual-edge and private factors indexed by \(\mathcal J=\mathcal E^{\leftrightarrow}(\mathcal G)\sqcup\mathcal V\sqcup\mathcal R\). Write
\[
L_{\mathcal G}=\left|\mathcal X_{\mathcal V}\times\mathcal X_{\mathcal R}\right|,
\qquad
K_{\mathrm{ub}}(\mathcal G)=L_{\mathcal G}+|\mathcal X_A|(|\mathcal X_Y|-1).
\]
There is a label-compatible deterministic response representation in which every factor has support at most the universal upper bound \(K_{\mathrm{ub}}(\mathcal G)\), the factors remain mutually independent, and, simultaneously for every full cell \((v,r)\) and every \((a,y)\in\mathcal X_A\times\mathcal X_Y\),
\[
P(V=v,R=r)=P_{\mathcal M}(v,r),
\qquad
P(Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(A=a))=Q_a^{\mathcal M}(y).
\]
statements.proof_tex:
Set
\[
L=L_{\mathcal G},
\qquad
D=(L-1)+|\mathcal X_A|(|\mathcal X_Y|-1),
\qquad
K_{\mathrm{ub}}(\mathcal G)=D+1.
\tag{1}
\]
Finiteness follows from \(\text{ass:finite-alphabets}\). The state spaces are nonempty because they are alphabets of the probability law induced by \(\mathcal M\), so every cardinality in (1) is a positive integer.

By \(\text{def:published-lm-class}\), \(\mathcal M\) is a measurable labeled-missingness SCM compatible with \(\mathcal G\). The proof below uses its finite endogenous alphabets but permits its exogenous factor spaces to be arbitrary measurable spaces.

We first derive the finite-dimensional barycenter reduction used below. Let \((\Omega,\mathcal A,\mu)\) be a probability space, let \(z:\Omega\to\mathbb R^m\) be bounded and measurable, and suppose \(z(\Omega)\) is contained in an affine subspace of dimension at most \(D\). Put \(b=\int z\,d\mu\). We claim that there are \(k\leq D+1\), points \(u_1,\ldots,u_k\in\Omega\), and weights \(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_k\geq0\) such that
\[
\sum_{i=1}^k\alpha_i=1,
\qquad
b=\sum_{i=1}^k\alpha_i z(u_i).
\tag{2}
\]
This is the needed Carath\'{e}odory reduction, which we prove here rather than invoke as an undeclared result.

Let \(S=z(\Omega)\), \(C=\operatorname{conv}(S)\), and let \(\overline C\) be its closure. Partition a bounded box containing \(S\) into finitely many disjoint Borel sets of diameter at most \(1/n\). From every set meeting \(S\), choose one point of \(S\), and replace each \(z(u)\) by the selected point in the same partition set. The resulting finite-valued map \(z_n\) is measurable, satisfies \(\|z_n-z\|\leq1/n\), and has \(\int z_n\,d\mu\in C\). Therefore
\[
b=\lim_{n\to\infty}\int z_n\,d\mu\in\overline C.
\tag{3}
\]

We show by induction on \(d=\dim\operatorname{aff}(\overline C)\) that the point \(b\) in (3) actually lies in \(C\). This is immediate when \(d=0\). If \(b\in\operatorname{ri}(\overline C)\), a sufficiently small relative Euclidean ball about \(b\) lies in \(\overline C\). Choose \(d+1\) points in that ball whose convex hull has \(b\) in its relative interior. Approximate those vertices by points of \(C\). Affine independence and strict positivity of the barycentric coordinates of \(b\) persist under sufficiently small perturbations, so \(b\) lies in the convex hull of the approximating points and hence in \(C\).

If instead \(b\) is on the relative boundary of \(\overline C\), choose \(x_n\in\operatorname{aff}(\overline C)\setminus\overline C\) with \(x_n\to b\). A minimizer \(p_n\in\overline C\) of \(p\mapsto\|x_n-p\|\) exists: a minimizing sequence may be restricted to a bounded closed ball, which is compact in the finite-dimensional affine hull, and \(\overline C\) is closed. Moreover, for \(x\in\overline C\), convexity places \(p_n+t(x-p_n)\) in \(\overline C\) for \(0\leq t\leq1\). Minimality gives
\[
0\leq
\|x_n-p_n-t(x-p_n)\|^2-\|x_n-p_n\|^2
=-2t\langle x_n-p_n,x-p_n\rangle+t^2\|x-p_n\|^2.
\]
Dividing by \(t>0\) and sending \(t\downarrow0\) proves the projection inequality
\[
\langle x_n-p_n,x-p_n\rangle\leq0
\qquad(x\in\overline C)
\]
directly. Since \(b\in\overline C\), minimality also gives \(\|x_n-p_n\|\leq\|x_n-b\|\), whence \(p_n\to b\). Normalize \(x_n-p_n\) and pass to a convergent subsequence on the unit sphere of the finite-dimensional direction space. Its limit gives a nonconstant affine functional \(\ell\) on \(\operatorname{aff}(\overline C)\) such that
\[
\ell(x)\geq\ell(b)
\qquad(x\in\overline C).
\tag{4}
\]
By linearity of integration and (4),
\[
0=\ell(b)-\ell(b)
=\int\{\ell(z(u))-\ell(b)\}\,d\mu(u).
\tag{5}
\]
The integrand in (5) is nonnegative, so it is zero almost surely. Restricting \(\Omega\) to this full-measure set leaves \(b\) unchanged and places the range of \(z\) in the proper exposed face
\[
\overline C\cap\{x:\ell(x)=\ell(b)\},
\]
whose affine dimension is strictly below \(d\). The induction hypothesis now gives \(b\in C\).

Thus \(b\) is a finite convex combination of points in \(S\). If a representation uses more than \(D+1\) positive weights, the corresponding augmented vectors \((1,z(u_i))\) are linearly dependent because the affine dimension of \(S\) is at most \(D\). Hence there are coefficients \(c_i\), not all zero, with
\[
\sum_i c_i=0,
\qquad
\sum_i c_i z(u_i)=0.
\]
After changing their common sign if necessary, some \(c_i>0\). With
\[
t=\min_{i:c_i>0}\frac{\alpha_i}{c_i},
\qquad
\alpha_i'=\alpha_i-tc_i,
\]
the new weights are nonnegative, sum to one, have the same barycenter, and at least one formerly positive weight is zero. Iteration proves (2).

We now apply (2) separately to each exogenous factor. By \(\text{ass:semimarkovian}\), the factors indexed by
\[
\mathcal J=\mathcal E^{\leftrightarrow}(\mathcal G)\sqcup\mathcal V\sqcup\mathcal R
\]
have a product law \(\bigotimes_{h\in\mathcal J}\mu_h\). The graph is finite, so \(\mathcal J\) is finite. By \(\text{ass:acyclic}\), the structural equations have a unique recursive deterministic evaluation
\[
\Phi(u)\in\mathcal X_{\mathcal V}\times\mathcal X_{\mathcal R}
\]
for each joint factor state \(u\). For \(a\in\mathcal X_A\), let \(\Phi^a(u)\) denote the evaluation after replacing only the equation for \(A\) by the constant \(a\). The equations for the missingness indicators are not replaced, in agreement with \(\text{def:causal-query}\).

Fix \(h\in\mathcal J\), temporarily holding the structural equations and all other factor laws fixed, and write \(\mu_{-h}=\bigotimes_{j\neq h}\mu_j\). Denote the model with these current factor laws by \(\mathcal M^{\circ}\). Define the bounded measurable vector
\[
\begin{aligned}
z_h(u_h)=\Bigg(&
\left(
\int \mathbf 1\{\Phi(u_h,u_{-h})=(v,r)\}\,d\mu_{-h}(u_{-h})
\right)_{(v,r)},\\
&\left(
\int \mathbf 1\{\Phi_Y^a(u_h,u_{-h})=y\}\,d\mu_{-h}(u_{-h})
\right)_{(a,y)}
\Bigg).
\end{aligned}
\tag{6}
\]
Measurability in (6) follows from Tonelli's theorem applied to the measurable nonnegative indicators. Its first block is a probability vector on the \(L\) full cells. For each fixed \(a\), its \(a\)-indexed outcome block is a probability vector on \(\mathcal X_Y\). Therefore every point in the range of \(z_h\) satisfies
\[
\sum_{(v,r)}z_{h,v,r}=1,
\qquad
\sum_{y\in\mathcal X_Y}z_{h,a,y}=1
\quad(a\in\mathcal X_A).
\tag{7}
\]
The equations in (7) concern disjoint coordinate blocks and are linearly independent. Consequently the affine dimension of the range of \(z_h\) is at most
\[
L+|\mathcal X_A||\mathcal X_Y|-1-|\mathcal X_A|
=(L-1)+|\mathcal X_A|(|\mathcal X_Y|-1)=D.
\tag{8}
\]

Product independence and Tonelli's theorem give
\[
\begin{aligned}
\int z_h(u_h)\,d\mu_h(u_h)
=\Big(&\bigl(P_{\mathcal M^{\circ}}(V=v,R=r)\bigr)_{(v,r)},\\
&\bigl(Q_a^{\mathcal M^{\circ}}(y)\bigr)_{(a,y)}\Big).
\end{aligned}
\tag{9}
\]
The second equality in (9) is exactly \(\text{def:causal-query}\), applied to the current product-factor model \(\mathcal M^{\circ}\). Applying (2) with the dimension bound (8) replaces \(\mu_h\) by an atomic probability measure supported on at most
\[
D+1=K_{\mathrm{ub}}(\mathcal G)
\tag{10}
\]
actual values of that factor, without changing any coordinate of (9). Since only one marginal factor law is changed, the new joint factor law is still a product law, so mutual independence is preserved.

Enumerate the finite set \(\mathcal J\) and repeat this replacement sequentially. At each step, define (6) using the marginal laws produced by all preceding steps. Equation (9) shows inductively that each replacement preserves the current entire full-data law and every interventional outcome coordinate; hence their values remain equal to the corresponding coordinates of the original model \(\mathcal M\). Let \(\widetilde{\mathcal M}\) denote the model after the last replacement. Then
\[
P_{\widetilde{\mathcal M}}(V=v,R=r)=P_{\mathcal M}(v,r)
\quad\text{for every }(v,r),
\tag{11}
\]
and
\[
Q_a^{\widetilde{\mathcal M}}(y)=Q_a^{\mathcal M}(y)
\quad\text{for every }(a,y).
\tag{12}
\]

Finally, relabel the selected support of factor \(h\) as \(\{1,\ldots,k_h\}\), where \(1\leq k_h\leq K_{\mathrm{ub}}(\mathcal G)\), and restrict the original structural equations to the Cartesian product of these selected factor values. All endogenous parent alphabets and all selected latent alphabets are finite, so these restrictions are deterministic response tables. If the fixed alphabet \(\{1,\ldots,K_{\mathrm{ub}}(\mathcal G)\}\) in \(\text{def:response-polynomial-fiber}\) is required, add zero-probability states and define every added state by copying one selected supported state in every structural equation incident to that factor. This padding leaves the support, product law, and all evaluations unchanged. By \(\text{ass:label-semantics}\), whenever a label requires omission of an observed parent in a context, the original mechanism is constant in that parent there; restriction and copying preserve this equality. Thus the tables are label-compatible. Their product factor law is mutually independent, and their acyclic evaluation agrees with the reduced model on every supported factor state. Equations (11)--(12) prove the claim. Since every full-cell probability is preserved, strict full-data positivity is preserved whenever it holds in the input model. No positivity, regularity, maximality, division, boundary limit, or additional support assumption is used in the reduction itself.

statements.statement:
Let an exact specialization on a negative partition cell yield \(\omega=(a,y,\theta^0,\theta^1)\) satisfying \(\mathsf W_j\). Decoding the two response vectors gives \(\mathcal M_0,\mathcal M_1\in\mathfrak F(\mathcal G,P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) such that
\[
P_{\mathcal M_0}(\mathcal O)=P_{\mathcal M_1}(\mathcal O)=P_{\mathrm{obs}},
\qquad
Q_a^{\mathcal M_0}(y)\neq Q_a^{\mathcal M_1}(y).
\]
The factors in both decoded models retain the individual-edge product structure and every full-data cell is strictly positive.
statements.proof_tex:
By the definition of \(\mathsf W_j\), for \(i=0,1\),
\[
\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}(\theta^i;P_{\mathrm{obs}})
\quad\text{and}\quad
q_{a,y}(\theta^0)\neq q_{a,y}(\theta^1).
\]
The converse direction of \(\text{thm:response-fiber-equivalence}\) decodes each \(\theta^i\) to \(\mathcal M_i\in\mathfrak F(\mathcal G,P_{\mathrm{obs}})\), preserves the product \(\prod_h\rho_h^i\), and gives
\[
Q_a^{\mathcal M_i}(y)=q_{a,y}(\theta^i).
\]
The observed-law equalities and strict positivity are conjuncts of \(\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}\). Substituting the last display into the query inequality proves every conclusion.

statements.statement: The formulas \(\mathscr P_{\mathcal G,A,Y}\) form a finite semialgebraic partition of the feasible projection \(\{\mathbf p:\exists\theta\,\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}(\theta;\mathbf p)\}\). For every compatible \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\), every \(a\), and every \(y\), the unique cell containing \((P_{\mathrm{obs}}(o))_o\) carries a unique value for \(q_{a,y}\) if and only if \(\mathcal M\mapsto Q_a^{\mathcal M}(y)\) is constant on \(\mathfrak F(\mathcal G,P_{\mathrm{obs}})\). Otherwise it carries \(\mathsf W_j\); under \(\operatorname{Exact}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\), a sample from \(\mathsf W_j\) decodes to the positive same-observed, different-query pair of \(\text{lem:negative-cell-model-pair}\).
statements.proof_tex:
For each \((a,y)\), \(\mathsf I_{a,y}(\mathcal G;\mathbf p)\) is a first-order formula over a real closed field whose atoms are polynomial sign conditions. By \(\text{lem:real-closed-field-quantifier-elimination}\), eliminating \(\theta^0,\theta^1\) produces an equivalent quantifier-free formula in \(\mathbf p\). Apply the same result to \(\exists\theta\,\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}(\theta;\mathbf p)\). Finiteness of the graph, the alphabets, the response-table set, and the universal finite factor supports makes this a finite family of polynomials. By \(\text{lem:finite-sign-invariant-cad}\), one finite sign-invariant CAD partitions Euclidean space into pairwise-disjoint semialgebraic cells on which every such sign, and hence every Boolean combination of the signs, is constant. Intersecting with feasibility and discarding empty cells gives the canonical finite partition
\[
\mathcal P_{\mathrm{feas}}
=\{\mathbf p:\exists\theta\,\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}(\theta;\mathbf p)\}
=\bigsqcup_{j=1}^J\{\mathbf p:\psi_j(\mathbf p)\}.
\tag{1}
\]
This uses only the feasibility and constancy formulas in \(\text{def:symbolic-observed-partition}\). By the revised \(\text{def:tcf-procedure}\), it is completed before trace enumeration, so later rational annotations cannot alter (1).

Fix a compatible \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\), write \(\mathbf p_{\mathrm{obs}}=(P_{\mathrm{obs}}(o))_o\), and fix \((a,y)\). Compatibility and the forward direction of \(\text{thm:response-fiber-equivalence}\) imply \(\mathbf p_{\mathrm{obs}}\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{feas}}\), so (1) gives a unique cell. Put
\[
\Theta(\mathbf p_{\mathrm{obs}})
=\{\theta:\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}(\theta;\mathbf p_{\mathrm{obs}})\}.
\tag{2}
\]
Unfolding \(\text{def:terminal-qe-test}\) gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathsf I_{a,y}(\mathcal G;\mathbf p_{\mathrm{obs}})
&\Longleftrightarrow
\neg\exists\theta^0,\theta^1
\bigl[\theta^0,\theta^1\in\Theta(\mathbf p_{\mathrm{obs}})
\wedge q_{a,y}(\theta^0)\neq q_{a,y}(\theta^1)\bigr]\\
&\Longleftrightarrow
q_{a,y}\text{ is constant on }\Theta(\mathbf p_{\mathrm{obs}}).
\end{aligned}
\tag{3}
\]
The two directions of \(\text{thm:response-fiber-equivalence}\) give surjective correspondence at the level of query values:
\[
\{q_{a,y}(\theta):\theta\in\Theta(\mathbf p_{\mathrm{obs}})\}
=\{Q_a^{\mathcal M}(y):\mathcal M\in\mathfrak F(\mathcal G,P_{\mathrm{obs}})\}.
\tag{4}
\]
Indeed, its forward direction puts the query value of every fiber model on the left, and its converse puts every value on the left into a decoded fiber model. Equations (3)--(4) prove the claimed equivalence of constancy.

If (3) is true, feasibility makes \(\Theta(\mathbf p_{\mathrm{obs}})\) nonempty, and
\[
\mathsf V_{a,y}(\mathbf p_{\mathrm{obs}},z)
\Longleftrightarrow
\exists\theta\in\Theta(\mathbf p_{\mathrm{obs}})
\,[z=q_{a,y}(\theta)]
\tag{5}
\]
therefore holds for exactly one real \(z\). If (3) is false, ordinary first-order semantics supplies \(\theta^0,\theta^1\in\Theta(\mathbf p_{\mathrm{obs}})\) with unequal query values. The conjunction asserting precisely these facts is \(\mathsf W_j\), so \(\mathsf W_j\) is satisfiable. Applying the converse direction of response-fiber equivalence separately to \(\theta^0\) and \(\theta^1\) yields
\[
\mathcal M_0,\mathcal M_1\in\mathfrak F(\mathcal G,P_{\mathrm{obs}}),
\qquad
Q_a^{\mathcal M_0}(y)=q_{a,y}(\theta^0)
\neq q_{a,y}(\theta^1)=Q_a^{\mathcal M_1}(y).
\tag{6}
\]
Membership in the fiber supplies strict full-data positivity, the exact common observed law, and individual-edge factorization. Neither (3) nor the decoding in (6) uses \(\operatorname{Exact}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\).

If exact input data are additionally supplied, \(\text{def:exact-observed-specialization}\) selects the cell and represents a satisfying pair by Thom encodings over the real closure of the ordered field generated by \(\mathbf p_{\mathrm{obs}}\). Then \(\text{lem:negative-cell-model-pair}\) gives the same properties in constructive form. This proves every assertion.

statements.statement:
Fix a compatible observed law \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) and a coordinate \((a,y)\). If the TCF cell containing \((P_{\mathrm{obs}}(o))_o\) is negative for that coordinate, then there exist \(\mathcal M_0,\mathcal M_1\in\mathfrak M_{+}^{\mathrm{rm}}(\mathcal G)\) such that
\[
P_{\mathcal M_0}(\mathcal O)=P_{\mathcal M_1}(\mathcal O)=P_{\mathrm{obs}},
\qquad
Q_a^{\mathcal M_0}(y)\neq Q_a^{\mathcal M_1}(y).
\]
Consequently \(Q_a(y)\) is not identified over the larger published ambient set \(\{\mathcal M\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{lm}}(\mathcal G):P_{\mathcal M}(\mathcal O)=P_{\mathrm{obs}}\}\). This existential conclusion does not require \(\operatorname{Exact}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\); exactness is required only to algorithmically extract a represented witness pair.
statements.justification: A finite-subclass witness is already an ambient-class witness, so negative TCF cells have a direct published-model interpretation.
statements.gap: The constructive exact-specialization interface is stronger than is logically needed for nonidentification; existential nonconstancy transfers without an exact representation.
statements.consumer: A negative ADHD medication or test-achievement coordinate certifies failure of ambient lm-SCM identification even when no numerical witness extraction oracle is supplied.
statements.proof_tex:
Let the cell containing \((P_{\mathrm{obs}}(o))_o\) be negative for \((a,y)\). By \(\text{def:terminal-qe-test}\) and \(\text{def:symbolic-observed-partition}\), the stored witness relation means that the real formula
\[
\exists\theta^0\,\exists\theta^1\,
\left[
\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}(\theta^0;P_{\mathrm{obs}})
\wedge\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}(\theta^1;P_{\mathrm{obs}})
\wedge q_{a,y}(\theta^0)\neq q_{a,y}(\theta^1)
\right]
\tag{1}
\]
is true. Choose a satisfying pair in the ordinary set-theoretic semantics of (1). This existence step does not require an effective representation of either response vector.

Apply the converse direction of \(\text{thm:response-fiber-equivalence}\) to each vector. It gives \(\mathcal M_0,\mathcal M_1\in\mathfrak F(\mathcal G,P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) with
\[
Q_a^{\mathcal M_0}(y)=q_{a,y}(\theta^0)
\neq q_{a,y}(\theta^1)=Q_a^{\mathcal M_1}(y).
\tag{2}
\]
By \(\text{def:observational-fiber}\),
\[
P_{\mathcal M_0}(\mathcal O)
=P_{\mathcal M_1}(\mathcal O)
=P_{\mathrm{obs}},
\qquad
\mathcal M_0,\mathcal M_1\in\mathfrak M_{+}^{\mathrm{rm}}(\mathcal G).
\tag{3}
\]
The membership definition \(\text{def:positive-rm-class}\) gives the inclusion
\[
\mathfrak M_{+}^{\mathrm{rm}}(\mathcal G)
\subseteq\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{lm}}(\mathcal G).
\tag{4}
\]
Thus the same two models are elements of the published ambient observed-law set. If \(Q_a(y)\) were identified on that set, it would be constant on it, contradicting (2). This proves ambient nonidentification. The exact-specialization interface in \(\text{def:exact-observed-specialization}\) is needed only when the algorithm must represent a satisfying pair by Thom encodings; it is not a premise of the existential inference from (1).

statements.statement: Every \(\xi\in\operatorname{DA4}(\mathcal G,A,Y)\) identifies the natural interventional law, and for every compatible observed law its value is \(f^{\mathrm{DA4}}_{a,\xi}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)=Q_a^{\mathcal M}(y)\).

statements.statement:
For every \(\mathcal G(H,m)\in\mathfrak G_{\mathrm{EIPFD}}\), every \(\mathcal M\in\mathfrak M_{+}^{\mathrm{rm}}(\mathcal G(H,m))\), every \(a\in\mathcal X_A\), and every \(y\in\mathcal X_Y\), writing \(h\) for a joint value of the always-observed logistics block \(H\),
\[
Q_a^{\mathcal M}(y)=
\sum_hP_{\mathcal M}(h)
\sum_{b\in\mathcal X_{B_1}}P_{\mathcal M}(b\mid a,h,R_W=0)
\sum_{a'\in\mathcal X_A}P_{\mathcal M}(y\mid b,a',h,R_W=0)
P_{\mathcal M}(a'\mid h,R_W=0).
\]
Every probability on the right is an observed-law probability.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(\mathcal G(H,m)\in\mathfrak G_{\mathrm{EIPFD}}\), \(\mathcal M\in\mathfrak M_{+}^{\mathrm{rm}}(\mathcal G(H,m))\), \(a\in\mathcal X_A\), and \(y\in\mathcal X_Y\).  Let \(Y(a)\) denote the outcome obtained by recursively evaluating the structural equations of \(\mathcal M\) after replacing the equation for \(A\) by the constant \(a\).  Thus \(P_{\mathcal M}(Y(a)=y)=Q_a^{\mathcal M}(y)\) by \(\text{def:causal-query}\).  By \(\text{def:positive-rm-class}\), the endogenous alphabets are finite and every full-data cell has positive probability.  Hence every nonempty marginal cell used below has positive probability, and all displayed conditional distributions are defined.

The graph in \(\text{def:endogenous-proxy-frontdoor-class}\) has the always-observed logistics DAG \(H\) as an upstream block whose only edge to the remainder enters \(R_W\).  Under \(\operatorname{do}(A=a)\), the edge \(R_W\to A\) is cut.  The semi-Markovian factorization in \(\text{ass:semimarkovian}\), with no additional unlisted edge leaving that block, then gives the counterfactual independences
\[
Y(a)\mathbin{\perp\!\!\!\perp}R_W\mid H,
\qquad
H(a)=H.
\tag{1}
\]
The second relation is also immediate from acyclicity because \(H\) is pre-treatment and has no parent descended from \(A\).  By the structural-intervention definition of \(Q_a^{\mathcal M}\), total probability, (1), and positivity of \(P(R_W=0\mid H=h)\),
\[
Q_a^{\mathcal M}(y)
=\sum_hP_{\mathcal M}(h)
P_{\mathcal M}(Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(A=a),h,R_W=0).
\tag{2}
\]

Now restrict to the context \(R_W=0\).  By \(\text{ass:label-semantics}\), the labeled arrow \(W\to A\) is absent in this context.  In the selected graph, \(B_1\) intercepts every directed path from \(A\) to \(Y\), because the only such route begins the chain
\[
A\to B_1\to\cdots\to B_m\to Y.
\tag{3}
\]
There is no open back-door path from \(A\) to \(B_1\): every edge entering \(B_1\) in the defined family is the arrow from \(A\).  Further, conditioning on \(A,H,R_W\) blocks every back-door path from \(B_1\) to \(Y\).  In particular, the path \(B_1\leftarrow A\leftrightarrow Y\) is blocked at the conditioned noncollider \(A\), as are paths entering \(A\) through \(Z\) before reaching \(W\leftrightarrow Y\).  These are precisely the ordinary front-door graphical conditions conditional on \((H,R_W=0)\).

Therefore the ordinary identification operations whose soundness is supplied by \(\text{lem:ordinary-id-soundness}\) yield, successively,
\[
P_{\mathcal M}(b\mid\operatorname{do}(A=a),h,R_W=0)
=P_{\mathcal M}(b\mid a,h,R_W=0),
\tag{4}
\]
\[
P_{\mathcal M}(y\mid\operatorname{do}(B_1=b),h,R_W=0)
=\sum_{a'\in\mathcal X_A}
P_{\mathcal M}(y\mid b,a',h,R_W=0)
P_{\mathcal M}(a'\mid h,R_W=0),
\tag{5}
\]
and, using interception in (3),
\[
P_{\mathcal M}(y\mid\operatorname{do}(A=a),h,R_W=0)
=\sum_{b\in\mathcal X_{B_1}}
P_{\mathcal M}(b\mid a,h,R_W=0)
P_{\mathcal M}(y\mid\operatorname{do}(B_1=b),h,R_W=0).
\tag{6}
\]
Substituting (5) into (6), and then the result into (2), gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
Q_a^{\mathcal M}(y)
=\sum_hP_{\mathcal M}(h)
\sum_{b\in\mathcal X_{B_1}}P_{\mathcal M}(b\mid a,h,R_W=0)
\sum_{a'\in\mathcal X_A}
P_{\mathcal M}(y\mid b,a',h,R_W=0)
P_{\mathcal M}(a'\mid h,R_W=0).
\end{aligned}
\tag{7}
\]
Every variable in (7) is always observed, except that \(R_W\) is itself an observed indicator.  No unobserved value of \(W\) or \(Z\) occurs.  By \(\text{ass:proxy-consistency}\), the joint and conditional probabilities in (7) are therefore probabilities of the observed record \(\mathcal O\).  This proves both the causal equality and observability assertion.

sampling_model.design: Population exact recovery from a known finite regular-maximal labeled-missingness graph, expressed as a symbolic semialgebraic partition of feasible observed-cell coordinates; graph discovery and finite-sample inference are outside the core.
sampling_model.units: Independent draws of the observed record \(\mathcal O\) are the eventual statistical input, while the identification theorems treat the observed cells as formal population parameters.
sampling_model.treatment: A supplied intervention value \(a\in\mathcal X_A\) for the substantive treatment \(A\).
sampling_model.overlap: Strict positivity of the finite full-data law ensures that every selected trace denominator used by the calculus is nonzero.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Not part of this exact-identification core; exact point specialization requires rational or algebraic cells with isolating data, or an exact-real sign oracle, and arbitrary population reals are not claimed to be computational inputs.

estimand_functional: On a partition cell identifying every outcome coordinate at \(a_0\) and \(a_1\), \(\tau_{s_Y}=\sum_{y\in\mathcal X_Y}s_Y(y)\{f_{a_1,j}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)-f_{a_0,j}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)\}\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Proposition 4 states that if \(K,H,\{L_r\}_r\) satisfy conditions \(\mathrm{(i)}\)--\(\mathrm{(v)}\), then equations \(\mathrm{(5)}\)--\(\mathrm{(7)}\) recover \(P(Y\mid\operatorname{do}(A=a))\) and the NATE as weighted context functionals.
Its algorithm is sound and complete when the context variables are observed causal roots.
Its search always terminates and any returned expression is correct, without a general completeness result.
Its partial-order recursion handles missing-data subproblems but leaves completeness for general DAG models open.
Any two valid fixing sequences for the same set yield the same reachable graph and kernel.
Definition 6 defines a hedge and Theorem 4 makes it a nonidentifiability witness; Theorem 6 and Corollary 2 connect recursive ID failure to that obstruction and establish completeness.
Finite discrete causal queries and evidence can be encoded as polynomial optimization problems over response functions.

tldr: Finite labeled-missingness graphs encode mechanism shifts caused by missing inputs, but existing NATE procedures can discard identifying information by restricting to a context before deriving an available kernel. The observed-law-indexed procedure \(\operatorname{TCF}(\mathcal G,A,Y,P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) works symbolically in the observed-cell coordinates and constructs a finite semialgebraic partition whose cells carry either a unique query functional or a non-singleton-fiber certificate formula. Its response-function variables preserve every individual bidirected-edge factor of the published semi-Markovian graph. An exact-law specialization may extract an algebraic pair, which an independent first-divergence theorem compiles into a colored hedge and two strictly positive same-observed, different-query lm-SCMs. TCF preserves the exact functionals of de Aguas et al. Proposition 4 and the Mokhtarian et al. root-control procedure and strictly contains both on the parameterized endogenous-indicator proxy front-door class, with \(\mathcal G_\star\) providing a fully worked delayed-selection member.

project_justification.gap: De Aguas et al. give a sufficient weighted-adjustment criterion and the Figure 3(b) fix-before-select recovery; Mokhtarian et al. give completeness only for observed root controls. CSI search, missing-data recursion, and ordinary hedges do not jointly preserve label licenses, proxy traces, strict positivity, and the individual-edge semi-Markovian factorization.
project_justification.niche: Finite positive regular-maximal lm-graphs admit exact observed-cell algebra, provided the response-function variables respect each bidirected edge rather than replacing an entire district by one unrestricted latent table. The missing graphical object is a reachable kernel carrying both its context license and its derivation trace.
project_justification.fill: The proposal supplies that colored kernel, a two-way edge-factorized response-function equivalence, a symbolic semialgebraic partition theorem with an exact-input specialization contract, a concrete finite CAD bound, soundness, and an independent first-divergence compiler establishing colored-hedge completeness. It preserves both published comparator functionals and proves strict containment through the explicit delayed-selection functional on \(\mathcal G_\star\) and its parameterized EIPFD family.

related_work: De Aguas et al. (2025), Proposition 4, equations \(\mathrm{(5)}\)--\(\mathrm{(7)}\), and Figure 3(b) are the first direct comparator: conditions \(\mathrm{(i)}\)--\(\mathrm{(v)}\) give a weighted context-adjustment functional, while Figure 3(b) exhibits fix-before-select information flow. Mokhtarian et al. (2022), Theorem 1, Corollary 2, and Algorithm 1, are the second theorem-level comparator: their context-by-context procedure is complete when context variables are observed causal roots. Theorem \(\text{thm:two-comparator-strict-extension}\) preserves both published functionals and strictly extends both on \(\mathfrak G_{\mathrm{EIPFD}}\); Proposition \(\text{prop:eipfd-star-worked}\) gives the complete edge list, delayed-selection front-door formula, and explicit failure of each comparator for \(\mathcal G_\star\). Tikka, Hyttinen, and Karvanen (2019), Algorithm 1 and Theorem 5, inform the terminating sound CSI search but do not supply general completeness. Bhattacharya et al. (2020), Proposition 1, informs recursive removal in selected and latent missing-data subproblems but does not carry lm-label traces. Richardson et al. (2023), Lemma 30 and Theorem 31, prove ordinary fixing-sequence invariance within one CADMG and kernel domain; \(\text{lem:colored-adjacent-swap}\) transports licenses and provenance. Shpitser and Pearl (2006), Definition 6 and Theorem 4, give the hedge and its nonidentifiability implication; Theorem 6 and Corollary 2 give the ID failure structure and completeness reduction used by the first-divergence invariant. Duarte et al. (2023), Proposition 2 and Theorem 1, inform finite response-function polynomialization; \(\text{thm:response-fiber-equivalence}\) supplies the lm-specific two-way equivalence absent from that general framework. Hwang et al. (2024) motivate propagating positivity through each identifying operation. Nabi, Bhattacharya, and Shpitser (2020) address full-law identification, whereas this target is query-specific NATE recovery.
technical_internal_limitation: The two high-risk steps are finite edgewise support reduction and the graphical converse. The compiler theorem must prove that every nonconstant fiber produces the stated first-divergent district invariant; only then does the Shpitser--Pearl forest argument extend to label licenses, recorded proxy histories, nonzero full-data cells, and individual-edge latent factorization. The symbolic CAD wrapper merely partitions the observed-cell parameter space and cannot substitute for that graphical proof. A shared district mixture is unavailable because it would violate the advertised semi-Markovian graph. The adjacent-swap lemma is local and does not claim that context restriction commutes with fixing; Figure 3(b) rules out that stronger statement.
honest_scope: The graph, labels, finite alphabets, outcome score map \(s_Y\), treatment, and outcome are supplied. Identification is stated symbolically over the feasible observed-cell coordinates and mathematically specialized to every nonempty finite-state, semi-Markovian, strictly positive, regular-maximal observational fiber. Numerical cell selection is defined only for rational or real-algebraic observed laws with isolating data, or through an exact-real polynomial-sign oracle; no ordinary computation on arbitrary population reals is claimed.
